## Closed

The last cycle's finished record, moved here whole by its closing commit and deleted by the next
opening ([Cycle-record](AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).

### fix: a cycle commit marks no rung current

#### Problem

(io-uring-x1's `m-13-0`, accepted at `m-13-1`, 2026-11-15) `cycle --commit` marks its own rung
`(done)` and the next `(current)`, a prediction written into history, made false by an inserted
rung, and already computed by `--status` and `--ladder`.

Running the cycle found two more (wink + agent, 2026-11-15 and 16):
- The rungs' states and the cycle's commits are inferred from the graph, the commits the cycle's
  bookmark reaches less those other bookmarks reach. A set-aside bookmark broke the inference
  twice: above the cycle it emptied the branch, and once the cycle moved past it, it cut the branch
  at its fork. The brittleness is the inference, not the revset.
- A cycle stopped early has no safe end. `--open` over a cycle in progress is undefined, a dead-end
  must land, and one left unlanded leaves the agent-repo's `ochid:` trailers naming work commits no
  pushed ref reaches.

#### Solution

A dead-end (wink, 2026-11-16). The cycle stopped after three rungs, since its fixes inferred what
should be recorded, and every change is reverted but this record, the Todo entries it filed, and
the version, which moves forward to `0.85.23`. The closing adds one thing, wink's at its review:
`agent-data/jj.md` names `jj diff --tool meld` for a side-by-side review, the agent-files draft
moving to `v0.3.1-14`. What was tried: the ladder writing `(done)` alone,
and a branch revset that a bookmark above the cycle no longer empties. What replaces it, in three
cycles filed in `## Todo`:
- **feat: a rung's state is recorded in TODO.md**, which carries m-13's fix.
- **feat: a closing names its shape, and its target once**.
- **feat: a dead-end lands on a target or a tag**.

The closing is also an experiment, today's dead-end path run end to end before the third of them
reshapes it: `cycle --close --multi-step --dead-end` as a trapezoid on `main`, landed.

#### Acceptance check

- In the tests, a `cycle --commit` writes its own rung `(done)` and no `(current)` anywhere in
  `zTOC.md`, `cycle --status` names the next rung, and a ladder holding an old `(current)` line is
  read and rewritten.
- In the tests, `cycle --rung-start` marks the rung `(current)` in the working copy, its commit
  holds it `(done)` with no `(current)`, and `--commit` without `--title` takes the rung in flight.
- In this cycle, the docs rung is started by `vc-x1-dev cycle --rung-start` and committed by
  `vc-x1-dev cycle --commit`, its working copy showing it `(current)` under review and its commit
  reading `(done)` for rungs 0 to 3 and the closing unmarked.
- `rg -F '(current)' AGENTS.md agent-data/ README.md` prints only the rationale's account of the
  change.

Result: not met, by the dead-end. Rungs 1 and 2 passed their own tests and are reverted, and the
checks move to the cycles that replace this one.

#### Deliberation

- **The next rung is unnumbered, as every rung not started is.** A number goes with a marker, so
  dropping `(current)` drops the next rung's number with it.
  - Numbering every rung was considered and is not done: the numbers would shift on every insert,
    the churn the marker change removes.
- **The grammar still reads `(current)`.** This cycle's own `zTOC.md` was written by `0.85.22`,
  and any workspace mid-cycle at an upgrade holds one, so a reader that refused it would stop the
  cycle it is upgrading.
- **The finding keeps its meaning.** A `(done)` rung below a rung not done is still a finding,
  named against the first rung not done rather than the current one.
- **A rung in flight is marked when it starts, by `cycle --rung-start`** (wink, 2026-11-15). A
  `(current)` written when work begins is a fact, and one written by the commit before was a
  prediction, so the marker returns in the working copy alone and no commit holds it.
  - `cycle --start` was considered and is not taken, reading too like `cycle --open`, wink's.
    `rung start` is a positional verb, which the scope-flags rule retired.
  - `cycle --commit` writing the next rung `(current)` into the new working copy was considered
    and is not taken: the work `@` would never be empty after a rung, against At rest.
  - m-13-0 set aside the working copy marking itself current, on the ground that committed trees
    would hold the marker. They do not, since the commit makes it `(done)`, and `m-13` is told.
- **The cycle is a dead-end, not trimmed and closed** (wink, 2026-11-16). Closing at the original
  scope, the docs rung finished, was considered and is not taken: its "no rung current" would be
  rewritten at once by recorded state's `current`, and rung 2's fix is partial.
  - Folding the redesign into this cycle as rungs was tried in the working copy and is not taken:
    the redesign is two problems and more than one cycle, and this cycle's subject is m-13's.
- **Everything is reverted but the record, its Todo entries, and the version** (wink, 2026-11-16).
  `main`'s tree is as it was at the opening, an experiment in what a landed dead-end leaves, and
  the record is kept, since a dead-end says what was tried, why it stopped, and what replaces it.
  - The version moves forward, not back to `0.85.22`, so no `0.85.23-N` is built twice with
    different code.
  - The side-by-side review is added at the closing's review, wink's, the one change `main` gains:
    `jj diff --from main --to @ --tool meld &` was how the closing was reviewed. The agent-files
    draft moves to `v0.3.1-14` for it, the set-aside's `-14` never committed.
  - The reverted code stays in the ladder's commits, for the replacing cycles to take back.
- **The set-aside docs rung stays local and unlanded**, `nruymrqm`, its bookmark deleted. No agent
  commit names it, so nothing dangles, and jj keeps it as a visible head.

#### Rungs

The rung subsections, in the ladder's order. The ladder itself is in `zTOC.md > ## Ladder`.

##### fix: a cycle commit marks no rung current opening

The cycle's first commit, carrying its plan: the bookmark, the last cycle's record deleted, and the
Todo entry moved into this block. It also carries wink's two Todo entries from the `t85-22`
testing, their titles' typos fixed, and the continuation notes reset.

`ladder_of` stops writing `(current)`, the finding is named against the first rung not done, the
grammar still reads `(current)`, and `--ladder`'s help, the tests, and `README.md` follow.
Reverted by the dead-end closing.

- The ladder marks a rung `(done)`, numbered, when a commit of its title is on the branch, and
  every other rung, the next included, is its link alone. `cycle --open`'s first ladder is the
  opening and the closing, neither marked, since it is made by the same function.
- The grammar reads `(current)` still, so a `zTOC.md` from an older `vc-x1` is a ladder and the
  next write drops the marker. The refusal's grammar names `(done)` alone, the form it asks for.
- The finding for a done rung below one not done names that rung rather than the current one.
- `README.md`'s `--status` specimen shows the titles unlinked, as the command prints them.

##### fix: a set-aside bookmark leaves the cycle's branch whole

(found 2026-11-15, setting the docs rung's edits aside) The branch was the commits the cycle's
bookmark reaches less those any other local bookmark reaches, so a bookmark above the cycle, the
set-aside Unplanned work asks for, reached every rung and emptied the branch: `--ladder` dropped
every `(done)` and `--status` counted no commit. Only a bookmark not above the cycle's own cuts the
branch now. Reverted by the dead-end closing.

- The revset subtracts what the other local bookmarks reach less those at or above the cycle's
  own, so `main` below the cycle still cuts it off and one at the same commit is left out as before.
- A test sets a commit aside with a bookmark above the opening and finds the opening still on the
  branch. Against the old revset it finds none.
- A `main` moved above a cycle in progress no longer empties the branch silently: what it brings
  is refused as commits that match no rung. Only cycles in progress read the branch, a landed one
  being found by `landed_bookmarks`, so a merge Land is untouched.
- `README.md` and `--ladder`'s help say a bookmark below the cycle's is what cuts the branch.
  `README.md`'s rung-marker paragraph, left with an overlong line by the last rung, is rewrapped.
- The fix is partial: once the cycle moved past the set-aside, its bookmark cut the branch at its
  fork, and `--status` counted one commit.

##### fix: a cycle commit marks no rung current closing

Closing out the cycle as a dead-end, landed on `main` as a trapezoid, its tree `main`'s but for
this record, its Todo entries, the version, and `agent-data/jj.md`'s side-by-side review, the

on a target or a tag**:
- The revert is by hand: `jj restore --from main` of every path but `TODO.md` and `zTOC.md`, and a
  bump of the version forward. A dead-end that reverts all would want the tool to do it.

content.content:
# Cycle model

A cycle's record shown as specimens rather than skeletons: the `config loader` cycle, a ladder
mid-run, and the `version flag` cycle, a single-step cycle after its closing. Copy the shape, not
the words. The rules are in [The In Progress block](notes.md#the-in-progress-block) and [Cycle
shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape).

Who writes what:

- `vc-x1 cycle --open --title` writes the scaffold: the title, the five item headings, the `##
  Todo` entry's text under Problem, the opening and closing rung subsections, and the ladder of
  the two in `zTOC.md`.
- The user and the agent write the rest, the planning being theirs: the items, and each work rung
  as a `#####` heading under `#### Rungs` with its intent, between the bookends.
- The tool makes the ladder from those headings, `cycle --ladder` and every cycle commit, each
  rung's number its position and each marker computed from the commits, so no marker is typed.
- `cycle --close` moves the block to `## Closed`, a single-step cycle's without its `#### Rungs`.

## A ladder, mid-run

The `config loader` cycle with its opening committed and its one work rung current, `TODO.md >
## In Progress`:

```
## In Progress

### refactor: extract config loader

#### Problem

Config parsing lives inside the CLI entry point, so every subcommand that wants a setting reaches
through `main` for it, and a test cannot load a config without building the CLI.

#### Solution

Move config loading into its own module with a single `load` entry point that the CLI and the tests
call alike.

#### Acceptance check

`cargo test` passes with a new test that loads a config from a fixture file without touching `main`,
and `vc-x1 validate-config` reports the same findings as before the move.

#### Deliberation

- One work rung, not two: the parser and the loader were going to be split first and moved second,
  but the move is what forces the split, so doing them together is fewer edits.
- The acceptance check compares `validate-config`'s output rather than asserting on internals, so a
  later rename inside the module does not invalidate it.

#### Rungs

The rung subsections, in the ladder's order. The ladder itself is in `zTOC.md > ## Ladder`.

##### refactor: extract config loader opening

The cycle's first commit, carrying its plan: the bookmark, the last cycle's record deleted, and the
Todo entry moved into this block.

##### refactor: split loader from parser

Loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load without parsing and a test cannot parse
without a file on disk.

##### refactor: extract config loader closing

Closing out the cycle.
```

The opening and closing subsections are the scaffold's, and the work rung's is the planner's,
written before its commit as an intent of a sentence or two. At the rung's commit the intent gains
its conceptual delta:

```
##### refactor: split loader from parser

Loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load without parsing and a test cannot parse
```

Run a cycle by its stages, each a flag, one command for the acts
the flow has.

--open opens a cycle: it makes the bookmark on the work @ first,
the slug of --title or --bookmark's name, kept local, then
writes the cycle's record. In TODO.md what `## Closed` holds is
deleted and the `## Todo` entry titled as --title is moved into an
`## In Progress` scaffold, an empty one when no entry matches, and
in zTOC.md the ladder is replaced with the opening and the closing.
Every check is made before anything changes: a cycle in progress is
refused, as is a name in use, and a workspace with no TODO.md or
zTOC.md, a cycle running on its record. --no-record makes the
bookmark alone, a branch the later stages will not take, as does
--bookmark without --title.
--dry-run says each edit and makes none. Nothing is committed or
pushed, and the version is the project's to bump.

--ladder makes the ladder in zTOC.md from the rung headings, the
`##### ` headings under `#### Rungs` of the cycle in progress in
TODO.md, in their order, so a rung is written once. Each line is
numbered by its position and its marker computed: `(done)` when a
commit of the rung's title is on the cycle's branch, `(current)` the
first without one. Refused, with nothing edited: a commit on the
branch that is no rung's, a rung written twice, a ladder not opened
and closed by the cycle title plus " opening" and " closing", and
a line of the ladder there that is no rung by its grammar. The
branch is the commits the cycle's bookmark reaches that no other
local bookmark does, the bookmark the title's slug or --bookmark's.

--commit commits the working copies as a rung of the cycle in
progress, by the code `vc-x1 commit` runs, so a dual workspace gets
the pair, each half stamped with the other's change id. A cycle's
first commit is its opening: the title is the cycle title plus
" opening" and the body `[opening] body`, a --body given taking
its place. Any other is a work rung, which gives --title, a rung
heading not yet committed, and --body, the text or @PATH. The ladder
is rewritten first, the rung done, so the commit carries it, and the
cycle's bookmark is the one advanced, no other. -s is required: `b`
the pair, `w` the work half alone, `p` a plain repo's commit, each
checked against the workspace. --push publishes the rung on the cycle's
bookmark, a
draft. The closing is not a rung's commit, and is refused.

--close [REV,...] closes the cycle from the work @, which is on the
cycle's tip, and names its shape, --single-step or --multi-step,
which the branch's commit count checks. --single-step is the cycle's
one commit: made now from @ when the branch has none, or the opening
with the closing squashed into it when it has one, its title the bare
cycle title and its trailer kept, and refused over two or more. Its
--body is required, the commit holding the work, unless
--default-body asks for the pointer. --multi-step is a ladder, whose
closing is its own commit, the cycle title plus " closing" and
`[closing] body` unless --title or --body is given, and refused with
no opening committed.
It is linear, on @'s own parents, unless --trapezoid <BOOKMARK> makes
the destination its first parent or a REV listed joins another
head, each a parent after @'s. --dead-end, with --multi-step, titles
the closing " dead-end closing". The ladder is rewritten, every
rung done, and the record moved to `## Closed`, both in the commit.
The acceptance check comes first, by hand, and again after.

--land <BOOKMARK> lands a closed cycle on the destination, any
bookmark, none assumed: the agent @
committed when the cycle's commits name it, the destination
fast-forwarded to the cycle's last commit, and the cycle's bookmark
deleted, --skip keeping a side. The cycle is the one `## Closed`
holds, its bookmark the title's slug or --bookmark's, and a cycle
still in progress is refused. A destination that moved is refused,
naming the ways on, and --merge is one: a merge commit of the
destination and the cycle's last commit, made from an empty @ and
then landed, a conflicted one undone and left to you. The stages
chain in their order, `cycle --close --multi-step --land <BOOKMARK> -s b
--push`, the
Land's checks made before the closing is. --push with --land
publishes the destination and deletes the cycle's bookmark on
origin, and without --land it is the draft push.

--push alone is a stage: it publishes what the cycle's state calls
for. A cycle in progress, or closed and not landed, is a draft, and
its bookmark is pushed. A cycle landed here publishes the target its
landmark is on and deletes the cycle's bookmark on origin, and with
nothing to publish it says so. -s is required, `b` or `p`.

--status says where the cycle stands and changes nothing: the
title, the bookmark and whether it is on the work @, the commits on
the branch and how many are not pushed, the ladder as the rungs and
the commits make it, a note when zTOC.md's differs, and the stage
that comes next. What another stage would refuse, it says.

The version is the project's, and no stage writes it. With `[version]
file` and `pattern` in the config, --commit and --close refuse a
commit that changes no line of the file starting with the pattern,
before anything is written, and --same-version commits it as it is.

-R is optional and says where, a workspace or a plain repo.

Usage: vc-x1 cycle [OPTIONS] <--open|--ladder|--commit|--close [<REV>...]|--land <BOOKMARK>|--status|--push>

Options:
  -V, --version...
          Version detail on stdout: -V the banner, -VV the full report (as
          `vc-x1 version`). Counted like -v/-vv.
          
          Both ride along: they print, then the subcommand runs, so one
          invocation captures the version and the command's output together.
          That is why this replaces clap's auto-version, which would exit after
          printing. Without either, the banner still prints, on stderr.

      --no-banner
          Suppress the banner stderr normally carries on every run.
          
          Only the ambient banner: an explicit `-V` still prints, since asking
          for it outranks suppressing it.

      --allow-jj-mismatch
          Run even when `jj -V` disagrees with our linked jj-lib.
          
          Per-invocation on purpose, never a config key: a key gets set once
          during a frustrating afternoon and then silently protects nothing.

  -v, --verbose...
          Verbose output: -v debug, -vv trace

      --log <LOG>
          Log file path (captures all levels)

      --title <STR>
          With `--open`, the bare cycle title, a Conventional Commit: the
          bookmark is its slug, and the record is written under it. With
          `--commit`, the rung's title, a heading under `#### Rungs`, and with
          `--close` the closing's, as written [default: the opening's for a
          cycle's first commit, and for a closing the cycle title, plus "
          closing" on a ladder]

      --body <STR|@PATH>
          The commit's body, the problem and its solution, or @PATH to read it
          from a file [default: `[opening] body` for a cycle's first commit, and
          `[closing] body` for a ladder's closing]

      --bookmark <NAME>
          The cycle's bookmark, in place of the title's slug: the name `--open`
          makes, and the one another stage reads the cycle's commits from and
          advances

  -s, --scope <SCOPE>
          Which repos, required with --commit, --close, --land, and --push:
          `w|work`, `b|both`, or `p|por`
          
          [possible values: work, both, por]

  -R, --repo <PATH>
          Where: a path in the workspace, its root or either repo, or a plain
          repo [default: the current directory]

      --dry-run
          Dry run: show what would be done without executing

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Stages:
      --open
          Open a cycle: make its bookmark on the work `@`, then write its
          record, `TODO.md`'s `## In Progress` scaffold and `zTOC.md`'s ladder

      --ladder
          Make `zTOC.md`'s ladder from the rung headings under `#### Rungs` in
          `TODO.md`, each marker computed from the cycle's commits

      --commit
          Commit the working copies as a rung of the cycle in progress, the
          ladder rewritten into it: the cycle's first commit is its opening, its
          title and body defaulted, and a work rung gives both

      --close [<REV>...]
          Close the cycle in progress from the work `@`, each REV listed another
          head joined, a parent of the closing: a branch with no commit or one
          is a single-step cycle, its closing squashed into its one commit under
          the bare cycle title, and a longer one gets the closing commit, titled
          and bodied by default. The record moves to `## Closed` in it

      --land <BOOKMARK>
          Land the closed cycle on BOOKMARK, the destination: commit the agent
          `@` when the cycle's commits name it, fast-forward the destination to
          the cycle's last commit, and delete the cycle's bookmark. After
          `--close` it lands the closing just made

      --status
          Say where the cycle stands: its title, its bookmark, the ladder with
          its markers, the commits not yet pushed, and the stages open from
          here. It reads, and changes nothing

      --push
          Publish. Alone, a stage: what the cycle's state calls for, its
          bookmark while it is a draft, and once landed here the target, the
          cycle's bookmark deleted on `origin`. With `--commit` or `--close`,
          the cycle's bookmark, a draft push, and with `--land` the target.
          Nothing is pushed without it

Close:
      --trapezoid <BOOKMARK>
          With `--close`, make the closing a trapezoid, a merge whose first
          parent is BOOKMARK, the destination, read where it is now [default:
          linear, the heads alone]

      --default-body
          With `--close`, give a single-step cycle's one commit the default
          body, `[closing] body`, a pointer at the record, in place of the
          `--body` it otherwise requires

      --dead-end
          With `--close`, close the cycle as a dead end: a closing commit, with
          `--multi-step`, its title ending " dead-end closing"

      --single-step
          With `--close`, required or `--multi-step`: the cycle is one commit,
          made now from the work `@` when the branch has none, or its opening
          with the closing squashed into it when it has one

      --multi-step
          With `--close`, required or `--single-step`: the cycle is a ladder,
          and the closing is its own commit above the opening and any work rungs

Open:
      --no-record
          With `--open`, make the bookmark alone and write no record

Land:
      --merge
          With `--land`, join a destination that moved by a merge commit, the
          destination its first parent and the cycle's last commit its second,
          made and then landed, a tree no rung validated [default: a destination
          that moved is refused]

      --skip <SIDE>
          With `--land`, which side of the cycle's bookmark is kept: `local`,
          `remote`, or `both`, none deleted

          Possible values:
          - local:  The local bookmark is kept, only `origin`'s deleted
          - remote: The remote bookmark is kept, only the local one deleted
          - both:   Both are kept, none deleted

      --delete-intermediate-bookmarks
          With `--land`, also delete the bookmarks on the commits strictly
          between the destination and the cycle's last commit, a stack of cycles
          landing together [default: named as merged and kept]

Commit:
      --same-version
          With `--commit` or `--close`, commit although the version's line is
          unchanged: with `[version] file` and `pattern` in the config, a commit
          that changes no line of the file starting with the pattern is
          otherwise refused

content.text:
Below is the full protocol. It folds in what the last session decided, which the dead-end filed as three Todo entries (recorded rung state, the shape and target named once, a dead-end on a target or a tag). It also folds in the set-aside Todo, zc-ring-x1's `m-14-0` (`--land` tags the version), and the three lessons in the dead-end's closing rung. Nothing is written to files yet. This is the deliberation, and it goes into the record at the opening.

# The cycle protocol, recorded state

## 1. The principle

`TODO.md` is the only source of truth for a cycle's state, and vc-x1 never infers state from the graph.
- Today the branch is "the commits the bookmark reaches that no other bookmark does", and that inference broke twice in the last cycle.
- The branch revset is dropped. The cycle's commits are the change ids its record holds.
- `zTOC.md`'s ladder is generated from the record by every cycle command and is never edited by hand.

## 2. The record format

Each `###` cycle heading and each `#####` rung heading may be followed by a TOML block:

````
### feat: extract config loader

```toml
bookmark = "feat-extract-config-loader"
```

#### Rungs

##### feat: extract config loader opening

```toml
state = "done"
change = "tolonzqsxkwmrnpzqvlotyysxuulnrkv"
```

The cycle's first commit, carrying its plan...

##### refactor: split loader from parser

```toml
state = "current"
```

Loading and parsing are one function...

##### refactor: move the CLI onto config::load

Not started, so it has no block.

##### feat: extract config loader closing
````

- **Cycle block.** `--open` writes `bookmark`, so no later stage needs `--bookmark`. The closing adds `state = "done"` or `"dead-end"`.
- **Rung block.** `state` is one of `current`, `done`, or `dead-end`. A `done` or `dead-end` rung also has `change`, its work commit's full change id, the same form `ochid:` uses.
  - A commit can carry its own change id, because jj fixes `@`'s change id before the commit and keeps it through a squash.
  - No rung number is stored. The ladder numbers rungs by position.
- **Where `current` lives.** Only the working copy holds `current`, because `--commit` turns it into `done`. No commit ever records a prediction.

## 3. Invariants, checked by every stage before it writes

1. **Order.** The ladder runs:
   - the opening first;
   - then the done and dead-end rungs, in commit order;
   - then at most one current rung;
   - then the rungs not started;
   - then the closing last.

   A rung can't be inserted above a done rung.
2. **Resolves.** Each recorded change resolves to exactly one commit, visible and not divergent, whose title is its rung heading.
3. **Chain.** Each rung's commit is the parent of the next rung's commit, and the last one is `@-`, the cycle's tip.
4. **Nothing unrecorded.** The revset `opening::@- ~ <recorded>` must be empty. That revset is anchored at the recorded opening, not at bookmarks, so a set-aside bookmark can't affect it.
   - A hand `jj commit` in the chain is refused, and the error names it with the fix (fold it in with `vc-x1 squash`).
   - Local-ladder intermediates are reported by `--status` as "not yet collapsed", and `--commit` refuses until they are collapsed.
5. **Done is frozen** (your rule). The heading and block of a `done` or `dead-end` rung equal what that rung's own commit holds. They are never deleted and never changed, and the prose under them stays editable.
   - A change is refused until it is restored.
   - Done rungs can't be renamed, even unpublished ones. That is stricter than today's rule, which only freezes published rung titles.
6. **Generated.** `zTOC.md`'s ladder must be the one built from the committed record or from the working copy's record. Any other ladder is a hand edit and is refused, and the fix is to edit `TODO.md`.
7. **Bookmark.** The cycle's bookmark is on the tip. If it has moved, that is reported.

## 4. The rung lifecycle

- **`--open`** works as today. It also writes the cycle block and marks the opening `current`.
- **`--rung-start`** marks a rung `current`, in the working copy only.
  - The rung is the first one not started, or the one `--title` names.
  - A named rung that is not next is moved up to be next, with its subsection.
  - `--title X --insert` adds a new heading as the next rung, so inserting an unplanned rung is one command.
  - It is refused when a rung is already current.
- **`--rung-stop`** returns the current rung to not started, and leaves the edits alone. This settles the Todo's open question: `current` is never in history, so it can always be undone.
- **`--commit`** commits the current rung, or the rung `--title` names.
  - It writes `state = "done"` and `@`'s change id, and rewrites the ladder.
  - With no rung in flight and no `--title`, it is refused rather than guessing.
- **`--commit --dead-end`** commits a rung that was given up, with its attempt kept in history and `state = "dead-end"`.
  - The tool then inserts and starts a rung `revert: <rung title>`, with `@` restored to the parent's tree except the record and the version file.
  - The revert gets its own reviewed commit, and the next rung's diff stays clean.

## 5. Unplanned work: set aside and take back

- **`--set-aside`** commits the working copy under the local bookmark `aside/<cycle bookmark>` and puts `@` back on the tip. One set-aside is allowed at a time.
  - The version file and the record files (`TODO.md`, `zTOC.md`) stay in `@`, so the take-back can't conflict on them.
- **`--take-back`** rebases the set-aside onto the new tip and deletes its bookmark.
- Because state is recorded, the set-aside bookmark no longer affects anything. It is just an address.

## 6. The closing

- **Shape named, target once.**
  - `--close --multi-step` requires `--trapezoid [<target>]` or `--linear`.
  - `--trapezoid` with no value takes the target from `--land`.
  - `--trapezoid A --land B` is refused.
  - `--linear` takes no target.
- **Shape checked.** The shape is checked against the count of recorded commits, not a revset.
- **A done closing** is refused while any work rung is current or not started. You finish it, dead-end it, or delete it, and deleting a rung not started is always allowed.
- **A dead-end closing, `--close --multi-step --dead-end [--revert]`:**
  - Rungs not started stay in the record unmarked, so the record shows how far the cycle got. Last time they were removed by hand.
  - A current rung is refused: commit it or stop it.
  - The tool renames the closing heading to `<title> dead-end closing` before the commit, which it may do because the closing is not done yet. That fixes last time's mismatch between the ladder and the commit title.
  - `--revert` restores the opening's parent tree into the closing, except the record and the version file. Last time that was done by hand with `jj restore`.
  - The version still moves forward.

## 7. How a cycle ends, and the next one begins

| # | How it ends | Durable by | Next cycle | `--yes` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `--close --multi-step [--dead-end] --trapezoid\|--linear --land <target> [--push]` | the target, and its version tag | `--open` | no |
| 2 | `--close --multi-step --dead-end --tag [<name>] [--push]` | the dead-end tag | `--open --from <target>` | no |
| 3 | `--close --multi-step --dead-end --no-tag` | nothing, until a tag is pushed | `--open --from <target>` | yes |
| 4 | nothing committed | nothing needed | `--open` | no |
| 5 | outside the tool (`jj abandon`) | none | anything | can't ask |

- **Version tag (`m-14`).** `--land <target>` tags the commit the target moves to as `v<version>`.
  - The version is read through `[version] file` and `pattern`, and an optional `[land] tag = "v{version}"` sets the form.
  - `--no-tag` skips the tag.
  - A tag already at the same commit does nothing. A tag at another commit is refused, and the error names both commits.
  - A workspace with no `[version]` gets no tag, and the tool says so.
- **Dead-end tag.** Named `dead-end-<ts>`, `<name>`, or `<name>-<ts>`, where `<ts>` is like `20261116T215837.123Z`. A name already taken, locally or on the remote, is refused.
  - `--tag-dead-end <rev> [<name>]` adds the tag afterwards, which turns row 3 into row 2.
- **Push carries tags.** A work-repo push also pushes the local tags `origin` lacks.
  - The tags are listed in the plan and in `--dry-run`, and they are pushed first.
  - A clash stops the push.
  - Only the work-repo is tagged. Agent commits always go on the agent `main`, so the agent side is durable once pushed.
- **`--open` over a cycle in progress** makes nothing. It prints rows 1 to 3.
- **`--open --from <target>`** starts the next cycle on the target after an unlanded dead-end (rows 2 and 3).
  - It prints the dead-end's version, and the opening commit is refused unless its version is higher, so no `X.Y.Z-N` is built twice with different code.
  - It brings forward the dead-end closing's `## Continuation notes`, `## Todo`, and `## Waiting`, so the Todo entries the dead-end filed are not lost. This works only when the target is still where the dead-end opened, and otherwise it is refused and the sections are carried over by hand.
- **Dangling-trailer warning.** An agent push lists the agent commits whose `ochid:` names a work commit no remote ref reaches (from rows 3 and 5), and pushes anyway.

## 8. Reports

- `--status` reads everything from the record: the ladder, which rung is in flight, the recorded commits not yet pushed, and any invariant that fails, with its fix.
- `--status`, the acquaint repo check, and `--open` all report a dead-end that is not durable. That is a visible head titled `* dead-end closing` that no remote ref reaches.
- Every new flag completes its values: the targets, the rung titles not started, the default tag name, and the dead-ends without a tag.

## 9. Migration

A cycle in progress whose record has no blocks is migrated once, by the first stage that runs. The done rungs get blocks from the old branch revset, the inference's last use, and an ambiguous migration is refused. Closed records are never migrated.

This cycle migrates itself. It opens under the old format, and once the recorded-state rung's dev build takes over, that build migrates the cycle's own record. We think that is the best test migration will get.

## 10. Agent-files, to `v0.3.1-15`

- **`AGENTS.md`:**
  - Cycle-record: the blocks, done is frozen, `zTOC.md` generated.
  - Cycle shape: the target named once, the closing's two forms, and the dead-end forms.
  - Unplanned work: `--rung-start --insert`, `--set-aside`, and `--take-back`.
  - The per-rung flow: a new step, `--rung-start`, before the work.
  - Close-out: steps 5 and 8, with tags.
  - The rules index: done is frozen.
- **`jj.md`:** the Land's tag step and the push carrying tags.
- **`notes.md`:** the In Progress block and zTOC format.
- **`cycle-model.md`:** the specimen with blocks, a dead-end rung, and an unlanded dead-end.

## 11. Considered and not taken, carried forward

- `zTOC.toml` or `zTOC.json` as the record: a second source of truth.
- Cutting the branch only at bookmarks not descending from the opening: still an inference.
- Storing rung numbers: they churn on every insert.
- `cycle --start` (reads too like `--open`) and `rung start` (a positional verb).
- `--push-dead-end`: `--push` is kept so a dead-end is reviewed before it is published.
- `--open` closing a cycle in progress as a dead-end: too easy.
- Stacking the next cycle on the dead-end: that lands it unasked.
- New: `--commit` falling back to the first rung not started is not taken, because a guessed rung is the bug this cycle removes.

## 12. Decisions for you

1. **One cycle or several.** I recommend one cycle, for three reasons:
   - The pieces share the record format and the invariants.
   - The agent-files change once, as a single docs rung.
   - Self-migration needs one cycle that runs across the format change.
2. **Dead-end rung.** An auto-inserted `revert:` rung, as I lean, or a `--revert` flag that leaves the revert in the next rung's commit?
3. **Tags.** Lightweight, through jj-lib, as I lean, or annotated? We think jj-lib can't make annotated tags, so they would need a git spawn, against the `clippy.toml` spawn register. The tagged commit's title already says what it is.
4. **Version tag on a landed dead-end.** I lean yes: the version moved forward, so `v<version>` is unique, even when `--revert` leaves an older tree.
5. **Set-aside.** Keep the record files in `@` (my lean), and is `aside/<bookmark>` the right name?

**Proposed title:** `feat: a cycle's state is recorded, and every end is durable`

**Proposed ladder:**
- opening
- `feat: a rung's state is recorded in TODO.md` (the format, the invariants, the generated `zTOC.md`, migration)
- `feat: cycle --rung-start, --rung-stop, and --commit by the rung in flight`
- `feat: a closing names its shape, and its target once`
- `feat: cycle sets a rung's edits aside and takes them back`
- `feat: a dead-end rung and a dead-end cycle revert`
- `feat: land tags the version, and a dead-end lands on a target or a tag`
- `feat: open over a cycle in progress, and open --from`
- `feat: reports name a dead-end not durable`
- `docs: the agent-files record a cycle's state`
- closing

The short form for ending a cycle stays a separate Todo, to be weighed once the long forms have been used.

The plain version: the cycle's state gets written down in `TODO.md` instead of guessed from the commit graph. Each rung records whether it is in progress, done, or abandoned, and which commit it is. Once written, a finished rung can't be changed. Every way of ending a cycle, finished or abandoned, leaves a pushed ref behind, either the target branch or a tag, and Land also tags the version for io-uring-x1. I've drafted all of it as one cycle of nine work rungs, and five questions above need your call before I write it into the opening.

Thoughts on your three points. I haven't changed anything.

## 1. The record and the repo

You're right, "never infers state from the graph" overstates it. By "graph" I meant the commit DAG (each commit's parent links) plus where the bookmarks point. The repo is the fact of what happened. The record can't overrule it, only be checked against it.

What actually broke last cycle was narrower. vc-x1 decided which commits belong to the cycle from bookmark reachability: the commits the cycle's bookmark reaches that no other bookmark reaches. That one inference is what should go. A restatement:

> The repo holds what happened. `TODO.md` holds where the cycle is going, and which commit each finished rung is. Every stage checks that the two agree, and a disagreement stops the stage. Neither side is assumed right.

In practice that means:
- **Done:** a rung marked `done` names a change the repo has, on the cycle's chain, with the rung's title.
- **Nothing extra:** the repo holds no commit between the opening and the tip that the record doesn't name.
- **Current:** `current` is the one marker the repo can't confirm, since it means "work has begun". It lives only in the working copy, so it is a statement of intent, not a claim about history.

So the record says what's planned and which commit is which rung. The repo confirms or refutes it, and vc-x1 never fills a gap by guessing.

## 2. A provisional bookmark, separate from the title

Recording the bookmark in the cycle block is what makes this work. Once vc-x1 finds the cycle's commits from the record, the bookmark is only an address. Its name can then be anything and change at any time.

- **`--open` needs nothing.** `vc-x1 cycle --open` makes a provisional bookmark, say `cycle-20261116T2215Z`, and a scaffold whose `###` heading is a placeholder. `--title` and `--bookmark` are both optional.
- **The title firms up later.** The cycle title is the `###` heading, editable until the opening is committed. The opening's commit refuses the placeholder, because its title is derived from the cycle title. Once committed, the opening's heading is frozen. The closing then pairs with the opening's title, and the `###` heading can still drift, the same way the current rule keeps the bookend pair's names.
- **Renaming at any time.** `--bookmark <new>` on any stage renames the bookmark (a `jj bookmark rename`, with the record updated), and `--rung-start --bookmark X` fits your per-rung idea.
  - The cost is only after a draft push. A rename then means deleting the old remote bookmark and pushing the new one, so it's a push and needs approval. Before any draft push it's free.
- **The quick test path you wanted:**
  1. `--open`
  2. `--commit`, which commits the opening, with its title given there
  3. `--rung-start --insert --title "feat: one"`, then work, then `--commit`
  4. Repeat step 3 for each rung.

  No ladder has to be planned up front, since `--insert` builds it as you go. The planned-ladder path stays the same, just optional.

## 3. Always a trapezoid

As I read it: each rung commit becomes the merge, with its first parent the base and its second the previous rung, and the previous rung goes back to one parent. The cycle is then a trapezoid at every rung, and linear is a choice made at the end.

What it buys:
- **Landable at every rung.** Ending early, a dead-end included, is just landing the tip.
- **Cheap rewiring.** The base is already an ancestor of the ladder, so the merge is redundant. Each tree stays exactly the rung's own, and `jj diff` of the tip still shows only that rung's change.
- **Nothing else moves.** Change ids survive the rewiring, so the record's `change` and the `ochid:` trailers stay valid.

What it costs:
- **A rewrite every rung.** Each `--commit` rewrites the previous rung, so its commit id changes. After a draft push, every rung means a forced push, and the rules refuse forced pushes from `cycle`.
- **The first parent must be pinned.** It has to be the base the opening started on, not the target where it is now. A target that moved would otherwise pull its changes into the mid-cycle trees. So the trapezoid would have to record its base, which is one more fact in the cycle block.
- **The closing still exists.** Its job is the record's bookkeeping, which the shape doesn't change.
- **Noise.** `jj log` shows a merge at the tip all through the cycle.

My lean is not to take it, and to get its benefit differently. "Landable at every rung" is really one command at any rung: `--close --multi-step [--dead-end] --trapezoid --land <target>`. That already makes the trapezoid when it's needed, with no rewriting along the way. If that command is reliable at any rung, the always-trapezoid shape adds rewrites without adding anything we can't already do. If you want it anyway, a reasonable form would be a cycle-block setting, `shape = "trapezoid"`, enforced only while the cycle has no draft push.

The plain version:
- The repo is the truth about what happened, and `TODO.md` says where we're going. vc-x1 checks the two agree instead of guessing.
- Because the record finds the cycle's commits, the bookmark is only a name, so it can be provisional at `--open` and renamed any time before it's pushed.
- Rungs can be added as you go, which makes a quick test cycle easy.
- Keeping the cycle a trapezoid at every rung would make it landable at any point, but it rewrites the previous commit every time. One reliable "close and land now" command gives the same thing more cheaply.

Agreed: the shape stays declared at the closing.

Got it on bookmarks. `--bookmark <new>` adds another bookmark, and `--bookmark-rename <new>` renames the cycle's own. Here's how I'd fit them in:

- **The cycle's bookmark.** There is exactly one, recorded as `bookmark` in the cycle block. `--open` makes it, provisional unless named. `--commit` advances it and `--land` deletes it.
- **`--bookmark-rename <new>`.** Renames the cycle's bookmark on any stage and updates the record. It's free before a draft push. After one, it's a push (delete the old remote name, push the new one), so it needs approval.
- **`--bookmark <new>`.** Adds a bookmark at the tip, or at `@` on `--open`. It's recorded as one more entry, `bookmarks = [...]`, so it's known to the cycle and doesn't affect which commits belong to it.
- **Old usage goes away.** Today `--bookmark` on a later stage means "which bookmark is the cycle", so stages like `--commit` and `--land` won't need it once the record holds the name.

Three things for you to decide about an added bookmark:

1. **Does it move?**
   - It could stay where it was made, marking a point such as "before the risky rung". That's what I lean toward, since the cycle's own bookmark already follows the tip.
   - Or it could advance with each rung, as a second name for the cycle.
2. **Does it get pushed?** With the cycle's bookmark on a draft push, or only when named?
3. **What happens to it at the Land?**
   - It could be deleted with the cycle's bookmark, which I lean toward.
   - It could be kept, as `--skip` keeps a side today.
   - Or it could be kept by default and listed.

The plain version: the cycle keeps one bookmark of its own, which moves with the work and can be renamed any time. `--bookmark` adds extra named markers alongside it. I'd have those markers stay put, be pushed only when you ask, and be removed at the Land, but that's your call.

content.text:
I agree. It's worth separating what's cheap from what's costly.

**Where the cost comes from.** A name isn't the problem. A new head is.
- A bookmark that sits on the cycle's chain, below the tip, is harmless. Its commit lands with the cycle, so the name just goes away at the Land.
- The cost starts when work grows from that bookmark. That creates a second head, with commits outside the record, and invariant 4 doesn't see them because they aren't between the opening and the tip.
- A head like that needs durability as soon as anything points at it. Once an agent commit names those work commits in its `ochid:`, the head has to be landed or tagged, or the agent-repo ends up citing commits that no remote keeps.
- So bushiness doesn't come from bookmarks. It comes from heads plus the agent's links to them, and every extra head is a durability obligation.

**What the flexibility you wanted actually needs:**
- **A provisional name, changeable any time.** `--bookmark-rename` covers it: still one bookmark, one head, and no new obligations.
- **Marking points in the cycle.** The record already does this. Each rung's `change` is a stable address that jj accepts anywhere a revision is wanted, and it survives rewrites. An added bookmark would be a second name for something already named.
- **Parallel work, a second head.** That's the costly case. Today's tools handle it explicitly: `--set-aside` makes one head, which nothing names and which is taken back before the closing, and `--close <REV,...>` joins other heads at the closing.

**My lean:**
- Take `--bookmark-rename`. Leave `--bookmark <new>` out of this cycle and file it as a Todo, to revisit if a real need shows up.
- Hold one rule for heads: vc-x1 makes a commit only on the cycle's chain, or on the one set-aside.
  - `--status` reports any other head that forks off the cycle.
  - `--close` refuses while a head that an agent commit names is not reachable from the closing or a pushed ref. Joining it with `--close <REV,...>` or tagging it clears that.
- That gives a clear rule for agent-made commits: either they land with the cycle, or they never get named by an agent commit.

The plain version: renaming the cycle's one bookmark is free, so take it. Extra bookmarks look cheap, but they invite side branches, and once the agent records links to commits on a side branch, that branch must be landed or tagged. The record's change ids already let us point at any rung, so I'd leave extra bookmarks out for now and add one rule: no commit off the cycle's line unless it's the set-aside or it gets joined or tagged before the closing.

content.text:
You're right. A set-aside is another head, the same bushiness. While it stays local it is only a convenience, and its real value appears once it's durable and can be picked up elsewhere. That makes it the same problem as the Todo **Work in progress is durable and continues on any machine**, which proposed a `wip/<bookmark>` ref on the remote.

**What "durable" needs for a set-aside:**
- **A remote bookmark, not a tag.** A set-aside changes: it's rebased when taken back, and maybe worked on elsewhere. A remote bookmark is durable until it's deleted, while a tag is meant never to move.
- **A name that ties it to its cycle.** For example `aside/<cycle bookmark>`. A draft push could carry it along with the cycle's bookmark.
- **Take-back on any machine.** Fetch, rebase onto the tip there, then delete the bookmark locally and on the remote. The delete is a push, so it needs approval. The rebase keeps the change id, so nothing that cites it breaks.
- **An agent side, possibly.** Continuing on another machine wants the session too, the agent `@` with its transcript and the continuation notes. That's exactly the `wip` Todo's case. A work-only set-aside is the narrower version.
- **The head rule still holds.** No agent commit names a set-aside until it has landed through a rung. That way, a set-aside deleted unlanded leaves no dangling `ochid:`.

**What I'd do with this cycle:**
- Take set-aside and take-back out of it. Their urgent reason was that a set-aside bookmark broke the branch inference. Recorded state removes that, so a hand set-aside (`jj commit`, a bookmark, `jj new` on the tip) becomes harmless again.
- Merge the two Todos into one, along the lines of **A parked head is durable and continues on any machine**. It would cover a work-only set-aside and the both-repos `wip`, as one mechanism: name, push, fetch, take back.
- Keep the head rule in this cycle, since it's what makes parking safe later. A parked head named `aside/*` or `wip/*` would be reported by `--status` as parked rather than as an unexpected fork.

That trims the ladder by one rung, leaving eight work rungs:
- `feat: a rung's state is recorded in TODO.md`
- `feat: cycle --rung-start, --rung-stop, and --commit by the rung in flight`
- `feat: the cycle's bookmark is provisional, renamed by --bookmark-rename`
- `feat: a closing names its shape, and its target once`
- `feat: a dead-end rung and a dead-end cycle revert`
- `feat: land tags the version, and a dead-end lands on a target or a tag`
- `feat: open over a cycle in progress, and open --from`
- `feat: reports name heads and dead-ends not durable`

Then the docs rung, `docs: the agent-files record a cycle's state`, and the closing.

The plain version: a set-aside is a side branch, and it's only worth the cost if it's pushed and can be picked up on another machine. That's the same job as the existing "work in progress continues anywhere" Todo, so I'd merge the two into one later cycle. This cycle would add only the rule that keeps side branches safe, plus a report of them.

content.text:
You're right about `--rung-start`, with one correction to the premise, and the `--commit` point turns up a gap in today's code.

**`--rung-start` and `--rung-stop` make no commits.**
- They only edit `TODO.md` and `zTOC.md` in the work `@`, so there's nothing to carry a trailer and nothing to make durable.
- `--rung-stop` simply undoes `--rung-start`. Throwing away the working copy drops both.
- Building a ladder on the fly costs nothing until a `--commit` records it, and that commit is what carries the rung's heading and block.

**A `--commit` with no agent work: today's code doesn't do what you describe.**
- In a dual workspace, `-s w` stamps `orepo:` and an `ochid:` naming the agent `@`. The test `work_stamps_a_bare_ochid_and_links` at `src/commit.rs:1436` shows it.
- That's a forward link. It assumes the agent's `@` will later become the commit that covers this work, by `commit -s a --covers` or at the Land.
- That fits the N:1 case, where an agent works across several work-only rungs. For a commit the user made alone, it falsely claims an agent partner.

**What I'd propose:**
- **An unpaired work commit.** In a dual workspace, a work commit with no agent link carries no trailer, and no agent commit is ever made to cover it. It needs its own scope, since `-s w` already means "work half now, agent later". Two ways to spell it:
  - a new scope value such as `-s u|unpaired`
  - a flag, `-s w --unpaired`

  I lean toward the scope value, since the scope is where every command already says which repos it touches.
- **Should the default follow who's typing?** Claude Code sets `CLAUDECODE=1` in its shells, so vc-x1 could tell whether the agent ran the command. I'd use that only as a guard, not to pick the default: in a Claude Code shell, `-s u` is refused unless the user asked for it. Your user-only commits stay trailer-free, and an agent can't quietly drop its links.
- **The Land already behaves correctly here.** It commits the agent `@` only when a cycle commit names it. So a cycle made entirely of unpaired commits makes no agent commit at the Land.
- **Durability gets simpler.** The dangling-link problem only exists where an agent commit names a work commit. An unpaired commit has no such link, so it can be kept or dropped (tagged, landed, or abandoned) without leaving anything dangling in the agent-repo. A user-only test cycle, like the one you wanted for done-to-current, therefore needs no durability rules at all.
- **The record doesn't need to say it.** Whether a rung was paired is visible from its trailers, so the rung block stays `state` and `change`.

The plain version: starting and stopping a rung only edits files in the working copy and makes no commit, so there's nothing to link or keep. A commit made without the agent shouldn't carry agent links. Today it does, because `-s w` promises an agent commit later. A new "unpaired" scope would make a commit with no links at all. Commits like that can be kept or thrown away freely, since nothing in the agent-repo points at them.

content.text:
**How `-s u` differs from `-s p`.** The commit they make is the same, one repo and no trailer. What differs is what each one says about the workspace.
- `-s p` (`por`) is for a plain repo, one with no agent-repo at all. It is refused on either side of a dual workspace (`src/common.rs:1290`), and the error points to `-s w`, `-s a`, or `-s b`.
- `-s u` would be for the work-repo of a dual workspace, committed on purpose without its agent partner.

The one-line answer for a user: **`p` means there is no agent-repo here; `u` means there is one, and this commit doesn't involve it.**

I'd keep them separate rather than letting `-s p` mean "unpaired" in a dual workspace. Today's refusal catches `p` typed in the wrong place, and a merged meaning would lose that check. It would also make the help ambiguous.

**A rung as any experiment, possibly with the agent's help.** That changes when pairing gets decided: at `--commit`, not at `--rung-start`.
- `--rung-start` doesn't know yet whether the agent will help, and it makes no commit.
- At `--commit`, the user picks the scope by what happened:
  - `-s b` if the agent helped: the pair, with trailers.
  - `-s u` if it didn't: no trailer.
  - `-s w` for the N:1 case: work now, the agent's commit to follow.
- **The durability obligation starts at the paired commit, not when the agent helps.**
  - Suppose the agent helped and the experiment is then thrown away before any commit. The agent's transcript mentions it, but no `ochid:` names anything, so dropping it is safe.
  - Once `-s b` commits it, an agent commit names that work commit. From then on the work commit has to stay reachable: it lands with the cycle, or is kept as a `dead-end` rung, or is tagged. It can't simply be dropped.

**A guard against the wrong choice, a warning rather than a refusal.**
- `--rung-start` records the agent `@`'s commit id in the rung's block.
- At `--commit -s u`, if the agent `@` has changed since then, a session wrote during the rung, and vc-x1 warns: "the agent-repo changed during this rung; if the agent helped, commit with `-s b`".
- This replaces my earlier `CLAUDECODE` idea, which only knew who typed the command, not whether the agent took part.
- The check isn't perfect. A session doing unrelated work also changes the agent `@`, which is why it should warn, not refuse.

The plain version: `-s p` is for a repo with no agent-repo at all, and `-s u` is for skipping the agent-repo in a workspace that has one. Whether a rung's commit gets agent links is decided when it's committed, by whether the agent actually helped. An experiment that is never committed can always be thrown away. Once the agent's commit links to a work commit, that work commit has to be kept. A warning at commit time would flag `-s u` when the agent-repo changed during the rung.

content.text:
The rung's block is the small TOML block directly under a rung's `#####` heading in `TODO.md > ## In Progress > #### Rungs`. It's the per-rung record from section 2 of the protocol. A rung that hasn't started has no block. `--rung-start` adds one, and `--commit` rewrites it:

````
##### feat: try the new parser

```toml
state = "current"
agent-at = "3f9c1e0a7b2d4c6e8f1a3b5c7d9e0f2a4b6c8d0e"
```

The rung's intent and prose...
````

After `--commit` it reads:

````
##### feat: try the new parser

```toml
state = "done"
change = "tolonzqsxkwmrnpzqvlotyysxuulnrkv"
```
````

How each key works:
- **`state`**: `current` is written by `--rung-start`, and `done` or `dead-end` by `--commit`.
- **`change`**: the work commit's change id, added by `--commit`.
- **`agent-at`**: the agent `@`'s commit id when the rung started.
  - It has to be the commit id, not the change id. The change id stays the same as the session writes, but the commit id changes on every snapshot, and that change is what the check looks for.
  - vc-x1 snapshots the agent `@` before reading it, both at `--rung-start` and at `--commit`, so the comparison is current.
  - `--commit` drops it once the check has run, because it means nothing in history. Only `state` and `change` end up in a commit.

Like `current`, `agent-at` only ever lives in the working copy.

The plain version: the "block" is a few lines of TOML under each rung's heading in `TODO.md`. They say where the rung stands and, once done, which commit it is. While a rung is in progress, the block also remembers what the agent-repo looked like when it started. The commit uses that to warn if the agent was active, then removes it.

Here's the revised protocol with every change so far. The changes from the first draft are marked **(rev)**.

# The cycle protocol, recorded state

## 1. The principle (rev)

The repo holds what happened. `TODO.md` holds where the cycle is going, and which commit each finished rung is. Every stage checks that the two agree, and a disagreement stops the stage. Neither side is assumed right.

- What goes is one inference: deciding a cycle's commits from bookmark reachability, the branch revset. The cycle's commits are the change ids its record holds, and the repo must confirm each one.
- `zTOC.md`'s ladder is generated from the record by every cycle command and never edited by hand.

## 2. The record format

A TOML block follows the `###` cycle heading, and another follows each `#####` rung heading that has started:

````
### feat: extract config loader

```toml
bookmark = "feat-extract-config-loader"
```

#### Rungs

##### feat: extract config loader opening

```toml
state = "done"
change = "tolonzqsxkwmrnpzqvlotyysxuulnrkv"
```

##### refactor: split loader from parser

```toml
state = "current"
agent-at = "3f9c1e0a7b2d4c6e8f1a3b5c7d9e0f2a4b6c8d0e"
```

##### refactor: move the CLI onto config::load

##### feat: extract config loader closing
````

- **The cycle block:**
  - `bookmark`: the cycle's one bookmark.
  - `provisional = true` **(rev)**: present while that name is vc-x1's placeholder.
  - `state = "done"` or `"dead-end"`: added by the closing.
- **The rung block:**
  - `state`: `current`, `done`, or `dead-end`.
  - `change`: the work commit's full change id, for `done` and `dead-end`.
  - `agent-at` **(rev)**: the agent `@`'s commit id when the rung started.
- **Working copy only.** `current` and `agent-at` exist only in the working copy. `--commit` replaces them, so a commit only ever holds `state` and `change`.
- **No numbers.** The ladder numbers rungs by position.

## 3. Invariants, checked by every stage before it writes

1. **Order.** The ladder runs:
   - the opening first;
   - then the `done` and `dead-end` rungs, in commit order;
   - then at most one `current` rung;
   - then the rungs not started;
   - then the closing last.

   No rung can be inserted above a done rung.
2. **Resolves.** Each recorded `change` resolves to exactly one commit, visible and not divergent, whose title is its heading.
3. **Chain.** Each rung's commit is the parent of the next one's, and the last is `@-`, the tip.
4. **Nothing unrecorded.** `opening::@- ~ <recorded>` is empty.
   - A hand `jj commit` in the chain is refused, and the fix is named.
   - Local-ladder intermediates are reported as "not yet collapsed", and `--commit` waits for them to be collapsed.
5. **Done is frozen.** A `done` or `dead-end` rung's heading and block match its own commit's. They are never deleted or changed, the prose stays editable, and a change is refused until restored. Done rungs aren't renamed, even unpublished ones.
6. **Generated.** `zTOC.md`'s ladder is the one built from the committed record or from the working copy's record. Anything else is a hand edit and is refused, and the fix is to edit `TODO.md`.
7. **Bookmark.** The cycle's bookmark is on the tip. If it has moved, that is reported.
8. **Heads (rev).**
   - vc-x1 makes commits only on the cycle's chain.
   - `--status` reports any other head that forks off the cycle.
   - `--close` refuses while a work commit named by an agent commit isn't reachable from the closing or from a pushed ref. Joining it with `--close <REV,...>` or tagging it clears the refusal.

## 4. Starting a cycle (rev)

- **`--open` needs nothing.**
  - With no `--title`, the scaffold's heading is a placeholder, `### (untitled)`.
  - With no `--bookmark`, the bookmark is provisional, `cycle-20261116T221500Z`, recorded with `provisional = true`.
  - Over a cycle in progress it makes nothing, and prints the ways to end it (section 8).
- **The title.** The `###` heading can be edited until the opening is committed. The opening's `--commit` refuses the placeholder.
- **The opening heading after the commit.** It's frozen, and the closing pairs with it. The `###` heading may still drift, as today's bookend rule allows.
- **A provisional bookmark follows the title.** When the opening commits, the bookmark is renamed to the title's slug and `provisional` is dropped. A name the user gave is never renamed.
- **`--bookmark-rename <new>`.** Renames the cycle's bookmark on any stage and updates the record.
  - It's free before a draft push.
  - After a draft push it's a push, deleting the old remote name and pushing the new one, so it needs approval.
- **Changed from today.** `--bookmark` on later stages, which today names the cycle, goes away, because the record holds the name.

## 5. The rung lifecycle (rev)

A rung is any piece of work or experiment, with or without the agent. `--rung-start` and `--rung-stop` edit `TODO.md` and `zTOC.md` in the work `@` and make no commit. That is how the rung shows up in the ladder while it's in flight.

- **`--rung-start`** marks a rung `current` and records `agent-at`.
  - The rung is the first one not started, or the one `--title` names, which is moved up to be next with its subsection.
  - `--title X --insert` adds a new heading as the next rung, so a ladder can be built as you go.
  - It is refused when a rung is already current.
- **`--rung-stop`** returns the current rung to not started and leaves the experiment's edits alone. Throwing away the working copy drops both.
- **`--commit`** commits the current rung, or the rung `--title` names.
  - It writes `state = "done"` and `@`'s change id, and rewrites the ladder.
  - With no rung in flight and no `--title`, it is refused.
- **`--commit --dead-end`** commits a rung that was given up, with its attempt kept in history and `state = "dead-end"`. Then the tool inserts and starts a rung `revert: <rung title>`, with `@` restored to the parent's tree except the record and the version file. *(Decision 2.)*
- **The quick test path:**
  1. `--open`
  2. `--commit --title "..."` for the opening
  3. `--rung-start --insert --title "feat: one"`, then the work, then `--commit`
  4. Repeat step 3.

## 6. Scopes and pairing (rev)

| Scope | Commits | Trailers |
|---|---|---|
| `b` | the pair | each half names the other |
| `w` | the work half now, the agent's to follow (N:1) | a forward `ochid:` naming the agent `@` |
| `a` | the agent half, `--covers <REVSET>` | one `ochid:` per work commit covered |
| `u` | the work-repo of a dual workspace, unpaired, never covered | none |
| `p` | a plain repo, with no agent-repo; refused on a dual workspace's sides | none |

- **`u` against `p`.** `p` means there is no agent-repo here, and `u` means there is one and this commit doesn't involve it.
- **Where `u` is taken.** `commit`, `squash`, `cycle --commit`, and `cycle --close`.
- **Pairing is decided at `--commit`, by what happened.** `-s b` if the agent helped, and `-s u` if it didn't.
- **The guard is a warning.** `-s u` warns when the agent `@`'s commit id differs from the rung's `agent-at`: "the agent-repo changed during this rung; if the agent helped, commit with `-s b`".
- **The Land** commits the agent `@` only for work commits with a forward `ochid:`. An unpaired commit has none, so a cycle made only of `-s u` commits makes no agent commit.
- **Durability.** The obligation starts at a paired commit. A work commit named by an agent commit must stay reachable from a pushed ref: landed, kept as a `dead-end` rung in a landed or tagged cycle, or tagged. Unpaired commits, and experiments never committed, can be kept or dropped freely.

## 7. The closing

- **The shape is declared at the closing (rev).** `--close --multi-step` requires `--trapezoid [<target>]` or `--linear`.
  - `--trapezoid` with no value takes the target from `--land`.
  - `--trapezoid A --land B` is refused.
  - `--linear` takes no target.
- **The shape is checked** against the count of recorded commits.
- **A done closing** is refused while a work rung is current or not started. You commit it, dead-end it, or delete it, and deleting a rung not started is always allowed.
- **A dead-end closing, `--close --multi-step --dead-end [--revert]`:**
  - Rungs not started stay in the record unmarked.
  - A current rung is refused.
  - The tool renames the closing heading to `<title> dead-end closing` before the commit, so the ladder and the commit title match.
  - `--revert` restores the opening's parent tree, except the record and the version file.
  - The version still moves forward.

## 8. How a cycle ends, and the next one begins

| # | How it ends | Durable by | Next cycle | `--yes` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `--close --multi-step [--dead-end] --trapezoid\|--linear --land <target> [--push]` | the target, and its version tag | `--open` | no |
| 2 | `--close --multi-step --dead-end --tag [<name>] [--push]` | the dead-end tag | `--open --from <target>` | no |
| 3 | `--close --multi-step --dead-end --no-tag` | nothing, until a tag is pushed | `--open --from <target>` | yes |
| 4 | nothing committed | nothing needed | `--open` | no |
| 5 | outside the tool (`jj abandon`) | none | anything | can't ask |

- **Version tag (`m-14`).** `--land <target>` tags the commit the target moves to as `v<version>`.
  - The version is read through `[version]`, and `[land] tag = "v{version}"` optionally sets the form.
  - `--no-tag` skips it.
  - A tag already at the same commit does nothing. A tag at another commit is refused, and both commits are named.
  - A workspace with no `[version]` gets no tag, and the tool says so.
- **Dead-end tag.** Named `dead-end-<ts>`, `<name>`, or `<name>-<ts>`, where `<ts>` looks like `20261116T215837.123Z`. A name already taken is refused. `--tag-dead-end <rev> [<name>]` adds the tag afterwards, turning row 3 into row 2.
- **Push carries tags.** A work-repo push also pushes the local tags `origin` lacks: listed in the plan and in `--dry-run`, pushed first, and a clash stops the push. Only the work-repo is tagged.
- **`--open --from <target>`** opens after an unlanded dead-end.
  - It prints the dead-end's version, and the opening is refused unless its own version is higher.
  - It brings forward the dead-end closing's `## Continuation notes`, `## Todo`, and `## Waiting`, but only when the target is still where the dead-end opened. Otherwise it is refused, and they are carried over by hand.
- **Agent push.** It lists the agent commits whose `ochid:` names a work commit that no remote ref reaches, and pushes anyway.

## 9. Reports

- **`--status`** reads everything from the record:
  - the ladder and the rung in flight;
  - the commits not yet pushed;
  - every failing invariant, with its fix;
  - the forked heads;
  - a dead-end that isn't durable.
- **The acquaint repo check and `--open`** report the last two as well.
- **Completion.** Every new flag completes its values: targets, rungs not started, the default tag name, and the dead-ends without a tag.

## 10. Migration

A cycle in progress whose record has no blocks is migrated once, by the first stage that runs. Its done rungs get blocks from the old branch revset, the inference's last use, and an ambiguous migration is refused. This cycle migrates itself once the recorded-state rung's dev build takes over.

## 11. Agent-files, to `v0.3.1-15`

- **`AGENTS.md`:**
  - Cycle-record: the blocks, done frozen, and `zTOC.md` generated.
  - Cycle shape.
  - Unplanned work: `--rung-start --insert`.
  - The per-rung flow: `--rung-start` before the work, and the scope chosen at the commit.
  - Committing vs pushing: the `u` scope.
  - Close-out: steps 5 and 8.
  - The rules index.
- **`jj.md`:** the Land's tag step and the push carrying tags.
- **`notes.md`:** the In Progress block and the zTOC format.
- **`cycle-model.md`:** the specimens with blocks, a dead-end rung, an unpaired rung, and an unlanded dead-end.

## 12. Considered and not taken

- `zTOC.toml` or `zTOC.json` as the record.
- Cutting the branch at non-descendant bookmarks.
- Storing rung numbers.
- `cycle --start`.
- `rung start`.
- `--push-dead-end`.
- `--open` closing a cycle in progress.
- Stacking on a dead-end.
- `--commit` guessing a rung.
- **(rev)** Always a trapezoid, with each rung commit the merge: it rewrites the previous rung every time, and a closing with `--land` gives "landable at every rung" without that.
- **(rev)** `-s p` meaning unpaired in a dual workspace: it loses the check that catches `p` typed in the wrong place.
- **(rev)** Defaulting the scope from `CLAUDECODE`: it says who typed the command, not whether the agent helped.

## 13. Filed as Todos, out of this cycle (rev)

- **`--bookmark <new>`, an additional bookmark.** Each one invites a side head, and the record's change ids already address any rung.
- **A parked head is durable and continues on any machine.** This merges `cycle sets a rung's edits aside and takes them back` with `Work in progress is durable and continues on any machine`. A set-aside is a head, and it's only worth its cost once pushed and resumable elsewhere. With recorded state, a hand set-aside becomes harmless meanwhile.

## 14. Decisions still yours

1. One cycle for all of this, which is my recommendation.
2. A dead-end rung's revert: an auto-inserted `revert:` rung, which I lean toward, or a `--revert` flag.
3. Tags: lightweight through jj-lib, which I lean toward, or annotated, which needs a git spawn.
4. A version tag on a landed dead-end: I lean yes.
5. The placeholder title `(untitled)` and the provisional bookmark `cycle-<ts>`: are those forms right?

## 15. Proposed title and ladder

**Title:** `feat: a cycle's state is recorded, and every end is durable`

**Ladder:**
- opening
- `feat: a rung's state is recorded in TODO.md`
- `feat: cycle --rung-start, --rung-stop, and --commit by the rung in flight`
- `feat: -s u commits the work-repo unpaired`
- `feat: the cycle's bookmark is provisional, renamed by --bookmark-rename`
- `feat: a closing names its shape, and its target once`
- `feat: a dead-end rung and a dead-end cycle revert`
- `feat: land tags the version, and a dead-end lands on a target or a tag`
- `feat: open over a cycle in progress, and open --from`
- `feat: reports name forked heads and dead-ends not durable`
- `docs: the agent-files record a cycle's state`
- closing

The plain version: the cycle's state is written into `TODO.md` and checked against the repo at every step. A cycle can start with no title and a temporary bookmark name, both firmed up later. Rungs can be added as you go, and starting or stopping one only edits files. A new "unpaired" scope commits work the agent didn't touch, with no links, so it can be kept or thrown away freely. Every way of ending a cycle leaves something pushed behind, the target branch or a tag. Five small decisions remain, and then this can go into the opening.

## Todo format

`TODO.md` has these sections, in this order. Each item in them is a short description with
reference links to more detail.

- `## Continuation notes`: where the agent was, for the agent that comes next. Ephemeral, never a
  record, `_None._` by default, written before a restart or a loss of context, and reset by the
  agent that reads it, after filing each fact into its home or keeping the bullet whose fact has
  none, so a reset never destroys the only copy of anything.
- `## In Progress`: the running cycle's record ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).
- `## Waiting`: important work that cannot start yet. Each entry names what it waits on and its
  rank once unblocked, and every opening checks the conditions.
- `## Todo`: entries in priority order, the first highest. The long-tail backlog is in
  [todo-backlog.md](../notes/todo-backlog.md).
- `## Ideas`: unranked.
- `## Bugs`: a pointer to [bugs.md](../notes/bugs.md).
- `## Closed`: the last cycle's finished record.
- `# References`: the file-local reference definitions, the file's last section ([Reference
  numbering](#reference-numbering)).

Every adopter has one `TODO.md` of this shape. It is not an agent-file, since its content is the
project's record, and `scripts/vc-dr-apply.sh` ships it as a skeleton: `## In Progress` reading
`_No cycle currently in progress._`, the other sections empty.

An entry is a `###` heading, its title, followed by its text. Priority is file order, the first
entry the highest, and reprioritizing is moving the entry. The title is unique within its file and
is the entry's anchor, so a citation is a link, `[title](TODO.md#<slug>)`, that the anchor check
verifies ([Prose form](prose.md#prose-form) for the text). Entries carry no number: a rank number
renumbers on every move and every citation that holds one goes stale, which is why the numbered
form was retired (2026-08-27). An entry's sub-entries, when it groups several, are bullets with a
bold title, cited by the bold text.

Example shape:

```
## Todo

### Add new feature X

The feature, in a sentence or two ([details](features.md#feature-x)).

### Fix bug Y

What is wrong and where [[1]].

[1]: bugs.md#bug-y
```

## The In Progress block

A cycle's record, `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, written at the opening
