## Thoughts for the future

Forward-looking design discussion lives in [`notes/forks-multi-user.md`](notes/forks-multi-user.md):
forking the dual-repo workspace, multi-user collaboration, multi-line `ochid:` trailers, bot-repo
size and scaling thresholds, URL-shaped per-user repos for distributed projects. Treat as a design
reference, not a status doc, and most of what's there is forward-looking, not yet implemented.

## Contributing

The tool's internal structure (module map, the CLI-args / ops-`Context`+`Params` split, the
subcommand model, and the two in-flight migrations) is described in
[ARCHITECTURE.md](ARCHITECTURE.md). Start there to orient.

The agent-facing cycle workflow (opening / commits / closing, the per-rung flow with `vc-x1
validate`, commit description shape, ochid trailers, pushing) is AGENTS.md's
[Cycle protocol](AGENTS.md#cycle-protocol).

The project's tasks, how to build, test, and install it, are in
[CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), with what an agent working here reads beyond the agent-files.

Bot-facing conventions are canonical in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) (hard rules + file map), its
`agent-data/` satellites, the project's layer [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), and a
workspace's local layer `custom.md`, gitignored:

- [Notes file conventions](agent-data/notes.md): Todo format, Reference numbering, Notes references
  (`[[N]]` citation style), Markdown anchor links, Retiring Done entries, and Chores conventions
  (section headers / Done entries exact-title rule, content rules, `Commits:` line format).
- [Prose form](agent-data/prose.md#prose-form): intro + bullets shape for long-lived prose (commit
  bodies, chores, doc comments).
- [Code conventions](agent-data/code.md): doc comments on every file / fn / method, `// OK: ...` on
  `unwrap*` calls.

Task tracking and release details: near-term tasks in [TODO.md](TODO.md), per-release details in
`notes/chores/chores-*.md`, and notes-specific formatting rules in
[notes/README.md](notes/README.md).

### No process spawns

vc-x1 runs jj and git through the jj-lib and gix libraries, never by spawning the `jj` or `git`
binaries, with one temporary exception named below. The ban is enforced, and the exceptions are
not: there is no allowlist. What exists is
three things, and it pays to know which is which.

- **The ban is config.** `clippy.toml` lists `std::process::Command::new` under
  `disallowed-methods`, and `Cargo.toml` sets that lint to deny, so a bare call anywhere fails
  `cargo clippy`, which `vc-x1 validate` runs.
- **An exception is an attribute.** Clippy has no way to list permitted sites, so the only grant

The line count of the agent-files, one row per landing that changed them, so the set's size is
tracked over time. A cycle that leaves the agent-files untouched adds no row, since a row saying
the count did not move records nothing. Smaller is the quasi-goal: a rule stated once is shorter

growing one is a prompt to ask what arrived as a paragraph that should have been a line. The count

# Agent-files size

The line count of the agent-files, one row per landing that changed them, so the set's size is
tracked over time. A cycle that leaves the agent-files untouched adds no row, since a row saying
the count did not move records nothing. Smaller is the quasi-goal: a rule stated once is shorter
than a rule stated three times, and a shrinking count is evidence the set is converging, while a
growing one is a prompt to ask what arrived as a paragraph that should have been a line. The count
is not a rule, and a rule is never cut to move it.

A finding from the proposal cycle (2026-08-27), for whoever next tries a cut: a draft that cut
AGENTS.md from 370 to 320 lines with every rule kept found that the remaining bulk is the rules
themselves, so a further cut has to cut rules, and that is a convention decision, not an edit.

The count is `wc -l` over `AGENTS.md`, `custom.md`, and `agent-data/*.md`, the total leaving out
`rationale.md`, taken at the close-out of a cycle that changed an agent-file and recorded here as
the closing rung's last edit, with the cycle title as the row's label. `rationale.md` is out of the
total because it is the rules' why and grows with every rule that gains one, so a rule gaining a
why does not read as the set growing. Rows before v0.2.5 counted it.

`vc-x1 agent-files size` takes the count and slides the per-file table, a new leftmost column in
and the oldest out. It is dry-run by default and `--no-dry-run` writes the file, `--label=TEXT`
names a column the set's version file cannot, and the `## Counts` row above stays a hand's work,
since its note is prose.

**Why they stay:**
- **They document vc-x1, not this project.** "Workspace config tables" is the schema of vc-x1's `validate`, `build`, `install` and `run`, which any workspace using vc-x1 can configure. A C project adopting vc-x1 would read them there. The values in the examples happen to be ours, but the section describes the tool.
- **This project's own values are already committed.** They're in `.vc-config.md`, so the fwlaptop gap doesn't apply to them, the way it did to `custom.md`.
- **Moving them now is churn.** The xtask cycle drops these four commands and the `[validate]`, `[build]`, `[install]` and `[profile.*]` tables from vc-x1. Their README sections get deleted then, and the definitions become xtask's code, summarized by CONTRIBUTING.md's `## Tasks`. If they moved now, they'd be written into CONTRIBUTING.md only to be removed one cycle later.

# Contributing

How to build, test, and change vc-x1, for a person or an agent. What vc-x1 is, and how to install
and use it, is in [README.md](README.md). How a change is made, the cycle and its commits, is in
[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#cycle-protocol).

## Tasks

The project's tasks, in the order a cycle uses them, a rung's loop first and Land after. A task is
named by its first column. Long output says whether it prints more than an agent's shell tool
returns, so an agent runs it in the [Long output](AGENTS.md#working-practices) form.

| Task | Command | When | Long output |
|---|---|---|---|
| bump | `cargo xtask bump X.Y.Z` | each commit of a cycle, to its version ([Suffix scheme](agent-data/versioning.md#suffix-scheme)) | no |
| validate | `vc-x1 validate` | fmt, clippy, and every test, at every rung before review | yes |
| validate fast | `vc-x1 validate --fast` | the unit tests only, while iterating | yes |
| test | `cargo test` | one test, or a filter of them | yes |
| clippy | `cargo clippy` | the lints alone | yes |
| build dev | `vc-x1 build --profile dev` | the dev build, into `target/debug`, without running | when cold |
| run dev | `vc-x1 run --profile dev` | `build dev`, then runs it, to try the change | when cold |
| install dev | `vc-x1 install --profile dev` | `build dev`, then copies it into `~/.cargo/bin` as `vc-x1-dev`, to try the change elsewhere | when cold |
| build | `vc-x1 build` | the release build, into `target/release`, at Land | when cold |
| run | `vc-x1 run` | `build`, then runs it, the smoke check before install | when cold |
| install | `vc-x1 install` | `build`, then reports it and copies it into `~/.cargo/bin`, at Land | when cold |

`cargo build` is long when cold too, and so are `jj log` without `-n` and a rung's `jj diff` or
`jj show`, which are no task's. What the build and install commands do, their profiles and where
each binary lands, is in [Build and install](README.md#build-and-install).

## Agents

What an agent working here reads beyond the agent-files, read at acquaint after `custom.md`
([Acquaint](AGENTS.md#acquaint)). It is the project's layer over the agent-files, committed, so every
clone has it, and a workspace's `custom.md`, local and gitignored, overrides it.

- Agent-files: vc-x1's are the `v0.3.1-15` draft of `### agent-files(proposal): v0.3.1` in
  [TODO.md](TODO.md), adopted locally (2026-11-03, `-1` and `-2` 2026-11-04, `-8` to `-10`
  2026-11-11, `-11` to `-13` 2026-11-13, `-14` and `-15` 2026-11-16). The proposal stays open.
- Messaging: the projects of the family message each other through the `../vc-x1-messages` repo,
  beside the work-repo, a clone of `https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1-messages.git`. A
  workspace without it clones it there. Its `README.md` is the protocol and it governs.
  - At an acquaint and at every cycle start the session does that README's Fetch action first,
    under its guards, and at acquaint reads what is pending for us, per its Read messages action.
  - A Fetch is asked for unless the workspace's `custom.md` gives a standing permission.

content.text:
Partly, yes. Most of what a continuation note carries is either a rule the agent-files should state once, or cycle state the record should hold. The agent-files can't hold this cycle's state, though. They're shared by every adopter and versioned, so "CONTRIBUTING.md is in review" can't live in them.

**What belongs where:**
1. **How to resume goes in the agent-files.** Two of the three gaps I listed are rule gaps, not missing notes:
   - **Uncommitted work on a cycle's bookmark is that cycle's rung in flight, not a finding.** The acquaint's repo check currently flags it unless a note accounts for it. A rule saying "the record accounts for it" removes the need for a note.
   - **A cycle with work in the `@` resumes at validate, then "please review".** Re-asking for review is cheap and always correct, so where a review stood doesn't need recording. The cold agent shows you the diff again. A review interrupted mid-iteration loses only the conversation, which is the agent-repo's anyway.
2. **Where a cycle stands goes in the record, written by the tool.** That's the protocol Todo's recorded state: each rung's `state`, `change` and `agent-at` in TOML blocks, plus the cycle's own block. It would also fix the third gap: if the cycle's block can say single-step, a single-step ladder stops showing the scaffold's bookends.
3. **What's left for continuation notes** is loose ends outside any cycle: the messages-repo items, an aside bookmark, the checks a Land asks the next session to make. Some of those could be Todo entries, and an aside bookmark becomes a parked head once that Todo lands. I think the notes would shrink to almost nothing, maybe to nothing.

**When.** The two resume rules fit the protocol cycle's agent-files rung, since recorded state makes them exact. Done now, they'd be a looser version.

**My recommendation:**
- Fold "resume from the record and the repo, not from notes" into the protocol Todo, as a principle and in its agent-files rung, and make "continuation notes shrink to loose ends" an explicit goal there.
- For this cycle, still write the one continuation note before you exit, since the rule doesn't exist yet.

Want me to add that to the protocol Todo?

The plain version: the agent-files should say how a cold session picks up a cycle, and the cycle's record should say where it stands. Then a session needs no hand-written note to resume. That fits the protocol cycle already planned. Until it lands, a short note covers the gap.

211	  `#####` rung heading once the rung has started.

215	    full change id for `done` and `dead-end`, and `agent-at`, the agent `@`'s commit id when the
216	    rung started, a commit id since it changes with every snapshot.
217	  - `current` and `agent-at` live in the working copy alone, `--commit` replacing them, so a commit

# Contributing

How to build, test, and change vc-x1, for a person or an agent. What vc-x1 is, and how to install
and use it, is in [README.md](README.md). How a change is made, the cycle and its commits, is in
[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#cycle-protocol).

## Tasks

The project's tasks, in the order a cycle uses them, a rung's loop first and Land after. A task is
named by its first column. Long output says whether it prints more than an agent's shell tool
returns, so an agent runs it in the [Long output](AGENTS.md#working-practices) form.

| Task | Command | When | Long output |
|---|---|---|---|
| bump | `cargo xtask bump X.Y.Z` | each commit of a cycle, to its version ([Suffix scheme](agent-data/versioning.md#suffix-scheme)) | no |
| validate | `vc-x1 validate` | fmt, clippy, and every test, at every rung before review | yes |
| validate fast | `vc-x1 validate --fast` | the unit tests only, while iterating | yes |
| test | `cargo test` | one test, or a filter of them | yes |
| clippy | `cargo clippy` | the lints alone | yes |
| build dev | `vc-x1 build --profile dev` | the dev build, into `target/debug`, without running | when cold |
| run dev | `vc-x1 run --profile dev` | `build dev`, then runs it, to try the change | when cold |
| install dev | `vc-x1 install --profile dev` | `build dev`, then copies it into `~/.cargo/bin` as `vc-x1-dev`, to try the change elsewhere | when cold |
| build | `vc-x1 build` | the release build, into `target/release`, at Land | when cold |
| run | `vc-x1 run` | `build`, then runs it, the smoke check before install | when cold |
| install | `vc-x1 install` | `build`, then reports it and copies it into `~/.cargo/bin`, at Land | when cold |

`cargo build` is long when cold too, and so are `jj log` without `-n` and a rung's `jj diff` or
`jj show`, which are no task's. What the build and install commands do, their profiles and where
each binary lands, is in [Build and install](README.md#build-and-install).

`validate`, `build`, `run`, and `install` run the commands `.vc-config.md`'s `[validate]`,
`[build]`, `[install]`, and `[profile.*]` tables give, described in [Workspace config
tables](README.md#workspace-config-tables).

## Agents

The project's tasks, in the order a change uses them. A change is made as a
[cycle](AGENTS.md#terminology): one commit, or a ladder of commits each called a rung, made on a
bookmark of its own and joined to `main` at the end, the Land. A task is named by its first column,
the name the agent-files use for it.

- Dev and release: the dev build is the quick debug one, for trying a change while it is made, and
  the release build is the optimized one installed as `vc-x1` at Land.
- Long output: whether the task prints more than an agent's shell tool returns, so an agent runs it
  in the [Long output](AGENTS.md#working-practices) form. "When cold" means only when cargo
  compiles everything, the first build after a clone or a dependency change.

| Task | When | What it does | Command | Long output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| bump | first, at each commit of a cycle | sets the version in `Cargo.toml` and refreshes `Cargo.lock`, `X.Y.Z-N` for a cycle's Nth commit and the bare `X.Y.Z` for its last ([Suffix scheme](agent-data/versioning.md#suffix-scheme)) | `cargo xtask bump X.Y.Z` | no |
| validate | before each review, and before every commit | formats the code, runs the lints, and runs every test | `vc-x1 validate` | yes |
| validate fast | while a review iterates | runs the unit tests only, changing no file | `vc-x1 validate --fast` | yes |
| test | to run one test, or the tests matching a filter | builds and runs the tests named | `cargo test [<filter>]` | yes |
| clippy | to see the lints alone | runs the lints, a warning failing it | `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` | yes |
| build dev | to build the change without running it | builds the dev binary, `target/debug/vc-x1` | `vc-x1 build --profile dev` | when cold |
| run dev | to try the change | builds the dev binary, then runs it with the arguments after `--` | `vc-x1 run --profile dev -- <args>` | when cold |
| install dev | to try the change from any directory | builds the dev binary, then copies it into `~/.cargo/bin` as `vc-x1-dev`, beside the installed `vc-x1` | `vc-x1 install --profile dev` | when cold |
| build | at Land, or to try the release build | builds the release binary, `target/release/vc-x1` | `vc-x1 build` | when cold |
| run | at Land, the check before install | builds the release binary, then runs it, `-- -V` printing its version | `vc-x1 run -- <args>` | when cold |
| install | at Land | builds the release binary, says what it will copy, then copies it into `~/.cargo/bin` as `vc-x1` | `vc-x1 install` | when cold |

`cargo build` is long when cold too, and so are `jj log` without `-n` and a rung's `jj diff` or
`jj show`, which are no task's.

# Contributing

How to build, test, and change vc-x1, for a person or an agent. What vc-x1 is, and how to install
and use it, is in [README.md](README.md). How a change is made, the cycle and its commits, is in
[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#cycle-protocol).

## Tasks

The project's tasks, in the order a cycle uses them, a rung's loop first and Land after. A task is
named by its first column. Long output says whether it prints more than an agent's shell tool
returns, so an agent runs it in the [Long output](AGENTS.md#working-practices) form.

| Task | Command | When | Long output |
|---|---|---|---|
| bump | `cargo xtask bump X.Y.Z` | each commit of a cycle, to its version ([Suffix scheme](agent-data/versioning.md#suffix-scheme)) | no |
| validate | `vc-x1 validate` | fmt, clippy, and every test, at every rung before review | yes |
| validate fast | `vc-x1 validate --fast` | the unit tests only, while iterating | yes |
| test | `cargo test` | one test, or a filter of them | yes |
| clippy | `cargo clippy` | the lints alone | yes |
| build dev | `vc-x1 build --profile dev` | the dev build, into `target/debug`, without running | when cold |
| run dev | `vc-x1 run --profile dev` | `build dev`, then runs it, to try the change | when cold |
| install dev | `vc-x1 install --profile dev` | `build dev`, then copies it into `~/.cargo/bin` as `vc-x1-dev`, to try the change elsewhere | when cold |
| build | `vc-x1 build` | the release build, into `target/release`, at Land | when cold |
| run | `vc-x1 run` | `build`, then runs it, the smoke check before install | when cold |
| install | `vc-x1 install` | `build`, then reports it and copies it into `~/.cargo/bin`, at Land | when cold |

`cargo build` is long when cold too, and so are `jj log` without `-n` and a rung's `jj diff` or
`jj show`, which are no task's. What the build and install commands do, their profiles and where
each binary lands, is in [Build and install](README.md#build-and-install).

`validate`, `build`, `run`, and `install` run the commands `.vc-config.md`'s `[validate]`,
`[build]`, `[install]`, and `[profile.*]` tables give, described in [Workspace config
tables](README.md#workspace-config-tables).

## Agents

What an agent working here reads beyond the agent-files, read at acquaint after `custom.md`
([Acquaint](AGENTS.md#acquaint)). It is the project's layer over the agent-files, committed, so every
clone has it, and a workspace's `custom.md`, local and gitignored, overrides it.

- Agent-files: vc-x1's are the `v0.3.1-15` draft of `### agent-files(proposal): v0.3.1` in
  [TODO.md](TODO.md), adopted locally (2026-11-03, `-1` and `-2` 2026-11-04, `-8` to `-10`
  2026-11-11, `-11` to `-13` 2026-11-13, `-14` and `-15` 2026-11-16). The proposal stays open.
- Messaging: the projects of the family message each other through the `../vc-x1-messages` repo,
  beside the work-repo, a clone of `https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1-messages.git`. A
  workspace without it clones it there. Its `README.md` is the protocol and it governs.
  - At an acquaint and at every cycle start the session does that README's Fetch action first,
    under its guards, and at acquaint reads what is pending for us, per its Read messages action.
  - A Fetch is asked for unless the workspace's `custom.md` gives a standing permission.

I agree, and I reworked the table along those lines. `validate --fast` passes.

**The columns are now Task, When, What it does, Command, Long output.**
- When is second. What it does says what changes, so for bump: "sets the version in `Cargo.toml` and refreshes `Cargo.lock`, `X.Y.Z-N` for a cycle's Nth commit and the bare `X.Y.Z` for its last".
- When no longer explains what the task does. For example, validate's When is just "before each review, and before every commit".

**The intro now defines the jargon** before the table uses it:
- cycle, rung and Land, in one sentence, linked to AGENTS.md's Terminology;
- dev versus release builds;
- what "when cold" means: only when cargo compiles everything, the first build after a clone or a dependency change.

**Some commands are now more specific:**
- `clippy` is the form validate runs, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- `test` shows its optional filter.
- The two `run` rows show `-- <args>`, and the release `run` row mentions `-- -V` as the check before install.

One thing that's yours to judge: the table is wide, five columns with long cells. It reads fine rendered, but the raw markdown rows are long, as the old ones were. If it still feels heavy, the next step would be a short section per task instead of a table.

message.content: What does "when cold" mean version "when hot", what's cold/hot?

content.text:
"Cold" and "hot" describe cargo's build cache in `target/`, not the command itself.

- **Cold:** `target/` doesn't yet hold compiled versions of the dependencies, so cargo compiles all of them. vc-x1 links jj-lib and gix, which is hundreds of crates and one output line each, so the output runs long. This happens on a fresh clone, after `cargo clean`, when `Cargo.lock` changes a dependency, after a Rust toolchain update, and the first time a profile is built.
- **Hot (or warm):** the dependencies are already compiled and cached, so cargo rebuilds only vc-x1's own crate. That's a few lines of output and a few seconds.

So "when cold" in the Long output column means the output is long only on that first, compile-everything build, and short on every build after.

"Cold" is build-system jargon and a neophyte won't know it, even with the definition in the intro. I'd change the column to say it plainly:
- Use **"first build"** in place of "when cold" in the cells.
- The intro would then say: "first build: long only when cargo compiles every dependency, after a clone, a `cargo clean`, or a dependency change, and short after".

Want me to make that change?

# Contributing

How to build, test, and change vc-x1, for a person or an agent. What vc-x1 is, and how to install
and use it, is in [README.md](README.md). How a change is made, the cycle and its commits, is in
[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#cycle-protocol).

## Tasks

The project's tasks, in the order a change uses them. A change is made as a
[cycle](AGENTS.md#terminology): one commit, or a ladder of commits each called a rung, made on a
bookmark of its own and joined to `main` at the end, the Land. A task is named by its first column,
the name the agent-files use for it.

- Dev and release: the dev build is the quick debug one, for trying a change while it is made, and
  the release build is the optimized one installed as `vc-x1` at Land.
- Long output: whether the task prints more than an agent's shell tool returns, so an agent runs it
  in the [Long output](AGENTS.md#working-practices) form. "When cold" means only when cargo
  compiles everything, the first build after a clone or a dependency change.

| Task | What it does | When | Command | Long output |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| bump | sets the version in `Cargo.toml` and refreshes `Cargo.lock`, `X.Y.Z-N` for a cycle's Nth commit and the bare `X.Y.Z` for its last ([Suffix scheme](agent-data/versioning.md#suffix-scheme)) | first, at each commit of a cycle | `cargo xtask bump X.Y.Z` | no |
| validate | formats the code, runs the lints, and runs every test | before each review, and before every commit | `vc-x1 validate` | yes |
| validate fast | runs the unit tests only, changing no file | while a review iterates | `vc-x1 validate --fast` | yes |
| test | builds and runs the tests named | to run one test, or the tests matching a filter | `cargo test [<filter>]` | yes |
| clippy | runs the lints, a warning failing it | to see the lints alone | `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` | yes |
| build dev | builds the dev binary, `target/debug/vc-x1` | to build the change without running it | `vc-x1 build --profile dev` | first build |
| run dev | builds the dev binary, then runs it with the arguments after `--` | to try the change | `vc-x1 run --profile dev -- <args>` | first build |
| install dev | builds the dev binary, then copies it into `~/.cargo/bin` as `vc-x1-dev`, beside the installed `vc-x1` | to try the change from any directory | `vc-x1 install --profile dev` | first build |
| build | builds the release binary, `target/release/vc-x1` | at Land, or to try the release build | `vc-x1 build` | first build |
| run | builds the release binary, then runs it, `-- -V` printing its version | at Land, the check before install | `vc-x1 run -- <args>` | first build |
| install | builds the release binary, says what it will copy, then copies it into `~/.cargo/bin` as `vc-x1` | at Land | `vc-x1 install` | first build |

`cargo build` is long when cold too, and so are `jj log` without `-n` and a rung's `jj diff` or
`jj show`, which are no task's. What the build and install commands do, their profiles and where
each binary lands, is in [Build and install](README.md#build-and-install).

`validate`, `build`, `run`, and `install` run the commands `.vc-config.md`'s `[validate]`,
`[build]`, `[install]`, and `[profile.*]` tables give, described in [Workspace config
tables](README.md#workspace-config-tables).

## Agents

What an agent working here reads beyond the agent-files, read at acquaint after `custom.md`
([Acquaint](AGENTS.md#acquaint)). It is the project's layer over the agent-files, committed, so every
clone has it, and a workspace's `custom.md`, local and gitignored, overrides it.

- Agent-files: vc-x1's are the `v0.3.1-15` draft of `### agent-files(proposal): v0.3.1` in
  [TODO.md](TODO.md), adopted locally (2026-11-03, `-1` and `-2` 2026-11-04, `-8` to `-10`
  2026-11-11, `-11` to `-13` 2026-11-13, `-14` and `-15` 2026-11-16). The proposal stays open.
- Messaging: the projects of the family message each other through the `../vc-x1-messages` repo,
  beside the work-repo, a clone of `https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1-messages.git`. A
  workspace without it clones it there. Its `README.md` is the protocol and it governs.
  - At an acquaint and at every cycle start the session does that README's Fetch action first,
    under its guards, and at acquaint reads what is pending for us, per its Read messages action.
  - A Fetch is asked for unless the workspace's `custom.md` gives a standing permission.

# Contributing

How to build, test, and change vc-x1, for a person or an agent. What vc-x1 is, and how to install
and use it, is in [README.md](README.md). How a change is made, the cycle and its commits, is in
[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#cycle-protocol).

## Tasks

The project's tasks, in the order a change uses them. A change is made as a
[cycle](AGENTS.md#terminology): one commit, or a ladder of commits each called a rung, made on a
bookmark of its own and joined to `main` at the end, the Land. A task is named by its first column,
the name the agent-files use for it.

- Dev and release: the dev build is the quick debug one, for trying a change while it is made, and
  the release build is the optimized one installed as `vc-x1` at Land.
- Long output: whether the task prints more than an agent's shell tool returns, so an agent runs it
  in the [Long output](AGENTS.md#working-practices) form. "First build" means long only when cargo
  compiles every dependency, after a clone, a `cargo clean`, or a dependency change, and short
  after, when it rebuilds vc-x1 alone.

| Task | What it does | When | Command |
|---|---|---|---|
| bump | sets the version in `Cargo.toml` and refreshes `Cargo.lock`, `X.Y.Z-N` for a cycle's Nth commit and the bare `X.Y.Z` for its last ([Suffix scheme](agent-data/versioning.md#suffix-scheme)) | first, at each commit of a cycle | `cargo xtask bump X.Y.Z` |
| validate | formats the code, runs the lints, and runs every test | before each review, and before every commit | `vc-x1 validate` |
| validate fast | runs the unit tests only, changing no file | while a review iterates | `vc-x1 validate --fast` |
| test | builds and runs the tests named | to run one test, or the tests matching a filter | `cargo test [<filter>]` |
| clippy | runs the lints, a warning failing it | to see the lints alone | `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` |
| build dev | builds the dev binary, `target/debug/vc-x1` | to build the change without running it | `vc-x1 build --profile dev` |
| run dev | builds the dev binary, then runs it with the arguments after `--` | to try the change | `vc-x1 run --profile dev -- <args>` |
| install dev | builds the dev binary, then copies it into `~/.cargo/bin` as `vc-x1-dev`, beside the installed `vc-x1` | to try the change from any directory | `vc-x1 install --profile dev` |
| build | builds the release binary, `target/release/vc-x1` | at Land, or to try the release build | `vc-x1 build` |
| run | builds the release binary, then runs it, `-- -V` printing its version | at Land, the check before install | `vc-x1 run -- <args>` |
| install | builds the release binary, says what it will copy, then copies it into `~/.cargo/bin` as `vc-x1` | at Land | `vc-x1 install` |

`cargo build` is long on a first build too, and so are `jj log` without `-n` and a rung's `jj diff` or
`jj show`, which are no task's. What the build and install commands do, their profiles and where
each binary lands, is in [Build and install](README.md#build-and-install).

`validate`, `build`, `run`, and `install` run the commands `.vc-config.md`'s `[validate]`,
`[build]`, `[install]`, and `[profile.*]` tables give, described in [Workspace config
tables](README.md#workspace-config-tables).

## Agents

What an agent working here reads beyond the agent-files, read at acquaint after `custom.md`
([Acquaint](AGENTS.md#acquaint)). It is the project's layer over the agent-files, committed, so every
clone has it, and a workspace's `custom.md`, local and gitignored, overrides it.

- Agent-files: vc-x1's are the `v0.3.1-15` draft of `### agent-files(proposal): v0.3.1` in
  [TODO.md](TODO.md), adopted locally (2026-11-03, `-1` and `-2` 2026-11-04, `-8` to `-10`
  2026-11-11, `-11` to `-13` 2026-11-13, `-14` and `-15` 2026-11-16). The proposal stays open.
- Messaging: the projects of the family message each other through the `../vc-x1-messages` repo,
  beside the work-repo, a clone of `https://github.com/winksaville/vc-x1-messages.git`. A
  workspace without it clones it there. Its `README.md` is the protocol and it governs.
  - At an acquaint and at every cycle start the session does that README's Fetch action first,
    under its guards, and at acquaint reads what is pending for us, per its Read messages action.
  - A Fetch is asked for unless the workspace's `custom.md` gives a standing permission.

lastPrompt: The "Agents" section of Contributing, how do agents find it?

content.text:
Agents find it through AGENTS.md. Nothing loads CONTRIBUTING.md on its own.

1. **Claude Code loads `AGENTS.md` automatically.** There's no `CLAUDE.md` here, and this session got AGENTS.md as its project instructions at start. Other agents that follow the AGENTS.md convention read it too.
2. **AGENTS.md sends the agent on.** Acquaint step 1 now says to read `custom.md`, then `CONTRIBUTING.md > ## Agents` when there is one. The rules index has the line "The project's layer", which links to the `## CONTRIBUTING.md` section.
3. **Both files are committed,** so a fresh clone has the pointer and its target. That's the fix for fwlaptop.

**The weakness:** it's an instruction, not an automatic load. It depends on the agent doing the acquaint. `custom.md` works the same way today, and it's been reliable because every session starts with "acquaint". Two cases are weaker:
- **A session that starts on a task without acquainting.** The auto-loaded AGENTS.md is in context, but nothing makes the agent open CONTRIBUTING.md.
- **After a context compaction.** AGENTS.md comes back in the reloaded instructions, but what the agent read from CONTRIBUTING.md survives only as the summary carries it.

**Making it automatic** would mean having the harness load it, for example a `CLAUDE.md` that imports both files. I'd hold off:
- I'm not certain how Claude Code treats AGENTS.md next to a CLAUDE.md, and I'd want to test it rather than guess.
- It only helps Claude Code. Other agents read AGENTS.md and wouldn't follow the import.
- AGENTS.md is shared by every adopter, so the import can't live in it.

I'd keep it as written for this cycle. If the uncertainty bothers you, I can file a Todo, "CONTRIBUTING.md is loaded with AGENTS.md, not just pointed to", to test the CLAUDE.md import later.

The plain version: the agent is told to read it at the start of every session, the same way it's told to read `custom.md`. It isn't loaded automatically. That's fine as long as sessions start with acquaint, and a Todo can explore auto-loading later.

message.content: I know how AGENTS find the agent-files in general I meant the "Agents" section in CONTRIBUTING.md.

content.text:
Sorry, I misread the question. An agent finds the `## Agents` section by its heading name, which AGENTS.md states in two places:

- **Acquaint step 1:** "when there is a `custom.md`, read it, then `CONTRIBUTING.md > ## Agents` when there is one".
- **The `## CONTRIBUTING.md` section:** "its `## Agents` is what an agent working there reads beyond the agent-files, read at acquaint after `custom.md`".

So the agent opens CONTRIBUTING.md and reads the section headed `## Agents`. That makes the heading a contract set by the agent-files: every adopter's CONTRIBUTING.md has to use exactly `## Agents` (and `## Tasks`), or the pointer misses.

**Where it's thin:**
- **AGENTS.md names the section but doesn't link it.** A link like `[CONTRIBUTING.md > ## Agents](CONTRIBUTING.md#agents)` would be clickable. But AGENTS.md is shared, so for an adopter without a CONTRIBUTING.md the link would be broken. That's why it's plain text.
- **CONTRIBUTING.md doesn't announce the section.** Its intro mentions the README and AGENTS.md's cycle protocol, but not that `## Agents` exists or that the agent-files read it by name. A person editing CONTRIBUTING.md could rename or fold the heading without knowing an agent depends on it.

**What I'd change in this cycle:**
- Add a sentence to CONTRIBUTING.md's intro: "`## Tasks` and `## Agents` are named by the agent-files, which read them by heading, so their names stay." That protects the contract where someone would actually break it.
- In AGENTS.md's `## CONTRIBUTING.md` section, state the contract once: "the two sections are found by their headings, `## Tasks` and `## Agents`".

Want both?

message.content:
My current thinking is CONTRIBUTING.md should be part of agent-files so a link should be durable. Different projects will have different

I agree on the result: every adopter's CONTRIBUTING.md has `## Tasks` and `## Agents`, so AGENTS.md can link `CONTRIBUTING.md#agents` and the link is always good. I'd make it required in the same way TODO.md is, though, rather than a member of the set.

**Why not a member of the set:**
- **The set is what adopters copy and diff.** `agent-files diff` compares each member between projects and `copy` carries them. CONTRIBUTING.md's contents differ in every project, so it would always show as different and must never be copied. That's the special handling `custom.md` already needs with `-c`.
- **TODO.md is the existing pattern.** AGENTS.md's Terminology says: "`TODO.md` is not one, since its content is the project's record, but the agent-files require that there is one, of the shape in Todo format." CONTRIBUTING.md fits exactly: required, its shape set by the agent-files, its content the project's.

**What that means for this cycle:**
- **Terminology** gains CONTRIBUTING.md beside TODO.md and zTOC.md: required, with at least `## Tasks` and `## Agents`.
- **AGENTS.md drops "when there is one"** and links for real: `[CONTRIBUTING.md > ## Agents](CONTRIBUTING.md#agents)` in acquaint step 1 and in the `## CONTRIBUTING.md` section, which states the shape. The rationale's "named conditionally" paragraph changes to say why it's required.
- **`scripts/vc-dr-apply.sh` writes a CONTRIBUTING.md stub** for a new repo, holding the two headings with a placeholder line each, as it already writes `TODO.md` and `zTOC.md`. Without that, a new repo starts out breaking the requirement. This moves the stub out of the xtask Todo and into this cycle, so I'd update that Todo too.
- **The other projects** take it at their next adoption. Until then their AGENTS.md is the old draft, so nothing breaks for them.

**Left for later:** a check that a CONTRIBUTING.md exists and has both headings, as an acquaint finding or part of `vc-x1 validate`. I'd file that as a Todo rather than add code here.

This grows the cycle by one script change. It still fits a single step to me, but it's your call. Go with this, stub in `vc-dr-apply` included?

The plain version: make CONTRIBUTING.md required, with two fixed headings, the way TODO.md is required, without making it one of the shared files. The links then always work, each project keeps its own content, and the new-repo script creates a starter file.

Strictly by links, there are 3 today, all in `agent-data/notes.md`. Counting files that are mentioned without a link, there are about a dozen.

**1. Live links to files outside the set: 3.**
- `notes/README.md` (notes.md:6)
- `notes/todo-backlog.md` (notes.md:73)
- `notes/bugs.md` (notes.md:75)

The other hits are examples inside code spans, not links that resolve: the `TODO.md#<slug>` ladder pattern, `features.md#feature-x`, `bugs.md#bug-y`, and the ladder specimen in `cycle-model.md`. CONTRIBUTING.md would make a fourth.

**2. Project files the agent-files rely on, named but not linked:**

| File | Mentions |
|---|---|
| `TODO.md` | 21 |
| `custom.md` | 16 |
| `zTOC.md` | 13 |
| `.vc-config.md` | 7 |
| `CONTRIBUTING.md` | 5 |
| `scripts/vc-dr-apply.sh` | 4 |
| `notes/done.md` | 4 |
| `notes/chores/` | 3 |
| `notes/README.md`, `notes/todo-backlog.md`, `notes/bugs.md` | 2 each |
| `notes/agent-files-size.md` | 1 |

**3. Examples only, nothing that has to exist:** `Cargo.toml`, `version.toml`, `pyproject.toml`, `src/`, `tmp/`, `tmp-durable/`, `jj-tips.md`.

**What category 2 really is.** Most of it is already a defined set of files: `scripts/vc-dr-apply-base/work/` ships `TODO.md`, `zTOC.md`, `custom.md`, `README.md`, `version.toml`, and `notes/` with `README.md`, `bugs.md`, `todo-backlog.md` and `agent-files-size.md`. So in practice there are three tiers:
1. **The set:** identical across adopters, diffed and copied. These are AGENTS.md and agent-data.
2. **The scaffold:** required to exist with a fixed shape, but each project fills its own content. That's `TODO.md`, `zTOC.md`, the `notes/` files, and now `CONTRIBUTING.md`. vc-dr-apply creates them, but nothing in the agent-files says they're required, except TODO.md and zTOC.md in Terminology.
3. **Local:** `custom.md`, gitignored.

**My suggestion.** Make tier 2 part of the agent-files by definition: members by existence and shape, not by content. Then a link into a scaffold file is "always valid" because the file is required. `agent-files diff` would check that the files and their required headings exist, not compare content, so `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s `## Tasks` and `## Agents` become part of that shape. That meets your rule that anything linked is a member, without making `copy` overwrite a project's own TODO.md or CONTRIBUTING.md.

That's bigger than this cycle: a Terminology definition, `agent-files diff`/`size` learning the scaffold, and a heading check. For this cycle I'd:
- add `CONTRIBUTING.md` to `vc-dr-apply-base/work/` as a stub with the two headings;
- name it in Terminology beside TODO.md and zTOC.md as required;
- make the AGENTS.md references real links;
- file a Todo: "the scaffold is part of the agent-files", covering the tier definition, diff checking shape, and the three `notes/` links.

Does that split work for you?

The plain version: only 3 links today point outside the shared files, all to `notes/` files that the new-repo script happens to create. The real gap is that "files every project must have, with its own content" isn't a defined category yet. I'd define it in a later cycle, and for now add CONTRIBUTING.md to the new-repo starter files and link to it.

get "copied" by those initialization operations. As a side note it's not correct we have to different mechanisms. Fine for the short term
but not acceptable in the long term, my current opinion.

content.content:
**`--adopt`**. Without it an existing TARGET is refused, named by what it holds. With it, init
grows the target into a dual workspace:

- A plain directory, no repo: both repos are created around it, and everything in it that its
  `.gitignore` does not exclude is the work repo's first commit, whatever the file sizes. Files
  over jj's new-file size limit (1MiB by default) are listed, since jj would otherwise leave them
  out. A `.gitignore` it already has is kept and given the lines it lacks, the agent directory's
  and `/.claude/settings.local.json`.
- A repo, jj colocated with git or git alone, with no workspace config: a git-only repo is
  colocated with jj first, its history kept. Its history stays, and one commit,
  "Adopt as a dual-repo workspace", goes on top, carrying `.vc-config.md`, the `.gitignore` lines,
  and the `ochid:` trailer to the agent repo's first commit. With an `origin`, the agent repo's
  remote is derived beside it, `--repo` and `--account` are refused, and the work side pushes
  nothing: the commit is yours to land. An agent remote init cannot create, one on a host other
  than GitHub, must exist, and is checked before anything is written. With no origin, the remotes
  come from `--repo` as for a fresh init, and both are pushed. A working copy with uncommitted work
  is refused, and a git-only repo's colocation is then taken back. A repo with no commit yet, as
  `cargo new` leaves one, has its content committed, as a plain directory has.
- With `--test-repo`, any of these is adopted as a test repo: its remotes are REMOTES, and an
  `origin` it has, on GitHub, another host, or a path, is replaced, its history pushed to
  `REMOTES/<name>.git`. The old `origin` is removed, or kept by `--upstream [NAME]` to fetch from,
  a NAME the repo has already being refused.
- A single-repo workspace, one whose config declares `repos.work` alone, such as `init -s por`
  makes: adopted as the repo above, except that its config is edited in place. `agent =` goes into
  `[repos]` and `agent-repo =` under `[remote]`, and every other line, prose and comments
  included, stays as it was.
- A dual-repo workspace is refused, having nothing to grow.

`--adopt` is refused with `-s por`, and on a `--target` that does not exist. The old `<TARGET> [NAME]` positionals are refused, naming `--target` and `--name`, and
`--por` is refused, naming `--scope por`.

content.content:
An entry is a `###` heading, its title, followed by its text. Priority is file order, the first
entry the highest, and reprioritizing is moving the entry. The title is unique within its file and
is the entry's anchor, so a citation is a link, `[title](TODO.md#<slug>)`, that the anchor check
verifies ([Prose form](prose.md#prose-form) for the text). Entries carry no number: a rank number
renumbers on every move and every citation that holds one goes stale, which is why the numbered
form was retired (2026-08-27). An entry's sub-entries, when it groups several, are bullets with a
bold title, cited by the bold text.

content.text:
I agree on both points. Here's what I found:

- **It's actually three mechanisms, not two:**
  - `vc-x1 init --adopt` makes the dual workspace: the repos, `.vc-config.md`, `.gitignore`. It copies no agent-files.
  - `scripts/vc-dr-apply.sh` copies the set (AGENTS.md, agent-data, licenses), the starter files in `scripts/vc-dr-apply-base/work/` (TODO.md, zTOC.md, custom.md, README.md, version.toml, `notes/` with four files), and a language skeleton.
  - `vc-x1 agent-files copy` copies the set alone, between adopters.
- **Nothing checks links across files.** `vc-x1 validate-anchors` checks same-file links only, and its help says "Cross-file targets are skipped". So today nothing verifies that an initialized repo's links resolve.
- **The three `notes/` links resolve today only by luck.** The files exist only because the starter files happen to include them, and the agent-files say nothing about that.

**What I'd do in this cycle** (it stays a single step):
- **Add `CONTRIBUTING.md` to the starter files** in `vc-dr-apply-base/work/`, a stub with `## Tasks` and `## Agents` and a line saying what goes in each. Then the new links resolve in a freshly applied repo.
- **Make it required in AGENTS.md's Terminology,** beside TODO.md and zTOC.md, with its two headings, and make the AGENTS.md references real links.
- **Acceptance check:** run `vc-dr-apply.sh` into a throwaway directory and check every link in the result resolves, files and anchors both. For now that's a small one-off script, since the checker doesn't exist yet.

**A Todo for the rest, `Initialization leaves no bad link`:**
1. **Links are checked across files.** `validate-anchors` follows links into other files and their anchors, and initialization runs it on its result. A link it can't fix is reported with the step that fixes it, for example "`custom.md` is local: write one if you need it".
2. **The starter files become part of the agent-files.** They move out of `scripts/` into the set's own tree, named as required with their shape. The copy then carries the information the links point to, rather than the links leaning on a script's directory.
3. **One mechanism.** `vc-x1 init` (with `--adopt`) takes on what vc-dr-apply does, and the script retires. `agent-files copy` stays as the update path between adopters, or folds in too. That's to settle in that cycle.

**Where the Todo goes is your call.** It touches `init`, which the xtask move also touches, through its `[validate]` table. I'd put it right after the xtask Todo and before the protocol one, so the next adoption, which will carry the protocol's agent-files, is the first to come out clean. That's a guess about order, though.

Go with this cycle's three additions and the Todo placed after xtask?

The plain version: right now three separate tools set up a project, and nothing checks that the links they leave actually work. For this cycle I'd add CONTRIBUTING.md to the files the setup script creates and test the result's links by hand. A follow-up cycle would add a real cross-file link check, move the starter files into the shared agent-files, and fold the script into `vc-x1 init`.

# Notes

Design notes that must outlast a cycle, one file per subject, linked from `TODO.md`.
Apply what SOURCE holds, one tree per repo, to the dual workspace DIR, made by `vc-x1 init`:

  SOURCE                a dual workspace, its agent repo found by its .vc-config.md
  SOURCE AGENT_SOURCE   a work repo and an agent repo, each given

  --to DIR         the workspace written [default: .]
  --landed         both repos at main, what landed, rather than the working copies
  --rev REV        the source work repo's commit, any jj revision naming one [default: @,
                   the working copy as on disk, which jj snapshots first]
  --agent-rev REV  the source agent repo's commit [default: @, as --rev]
  --skel DIR       the skeletons, a directory holding vc-dr-apply-base/ and vc-dr-apply-lang/,
                   as on disk [default: the source work repo's scripts/ at --rev, else this
                   script's own directory, symlinks resolved]
  --lang NAME      also apply the language skeleton vc-dr-apply-lang/NAME/, its [validate]
                   table appended to DIR's .vc-config.md; --lang alone lists them
  --dry-run        print the plan and write nothing

The default is the active version, the working copy with what it has not committed, so a test
repo gets the rules being worked on. --landed takes the trunk's, and --rev or --agent-rev, given
after it, overrides it for that repo. The skeletons follow the work repo's revision, so they
match the agent-files they come with.

From the work repo: AGENTS.md, agent-data/, and LICENSE-*. From the agent repo: LICENSE-*,
README.md, its first line renamed for DIR's agent repo, and memory/MEMORY.md, each when present.
From vc-dr-apply-base/: work/, the work repo's skeletons, {name} the workspace's directory name
and {module} it with each '-' an '_', in file contents and paths, and gitignore-lines, the
.gitignore lines.

A language skeleton, vc-dr-apply-lang/NAME/, holds the project's starting files, written like the
others, and three files that are not: validate.toml, the [validate] table appended to
.vc-config.md, refused when it has one already; gitignore-lines, more .gitignore lines; and
replaces, the base skeleton's paths it supersedes, left out, version.toml when the build system
holds the version. A new language is a new directory with a validate.toml.

Both repos of DIR must have an empty `@`, so every write is a diff `jj restore` undoes. Each
path is new, identical, or differs, judged on disk. New is written and identical skipped, and
any path that differs refuses the whole apply, nothing written. `.gitignore` takes the lines it
lacks. Nothing is committed: the end names the commit to make after review.
EOF
}

  --lang NAME      also apply the language skeleton vc-dr-apply-lang/NAME/, its [validate]
                   table appended to DIR's .vc-config.md; --lang alone lists them
  --dry-run        print the plan and write nothing

The default is the active version, the working copy with what it has not committed, so a test
repo gets the rules being worked on. --landed takes the trunk's, and --rev or --agent-rev, given
after it, overrides it for that repo. The skeletons follow the work repo's revision, so they
match the agent-files they come with.

From the work repo: AGENTS.md, agent-data/, and LICENSE-*. From the agent repo: LICENSE-*,
README.md, its first line renamed for DIR's agent repo, and memory/MEMORY.md, each when present.
From vc-dr-apply-base/: work/, the work repo's skeletons, {name} the workspace's directory name
and {module} it with each '-' an '_', in file contents and paths, and gitignore-lines, the
.gitignore lines.

A language skeleton, vc-dr-apply-lang/NAME/, holds the project's starting files, written like the
others, and three files that are not: validate.toml, the [validate] table appended to
.vc-config.md, refused when it has one already; gitignore-lines, more .gitignore lines; and
replaces, the base skeleton's paths it supersedes, left out, version.toml when the build system
holds the version. A new language is a new directory with a validate.toml.

Both repos of DIR must have an empty `@`, so every write is a diff `jj restore` undoes. Each
path is new, identical, or differs, judged on disk. New is written and identical skipped, and
any path that differs refuses the whole apply, nothing written. `.gitignore` takes the lines it
lacks. Nothing is committed: the end names the commit to make after review.
EOF
}

"""Check cross-file markdown links under a root: each target file exists, and its anchor is a heading.

Usage: python3 -I xlinks.py ROOT
Skips fenced code blocks, inline code spans, http(s)/mailto links, and same-file `#anchor` links
(vc-x1 validate-anchors covers those). Slugs follow GitHub's rule: lowercase, punctuation other
than '-' and '_' dropped, spaces to '-', and repeats numbered -1, -2, ...
"""
import os
import re
import sys

root = os.path.abspath(sys.argv[1])


def slugs(path):
    out, seen, fence = set(), {}, False
    for line in open(path, encoding="utf-8"):
        if line.lstrip().startswith("```"):
            fence = not fence
            continue
        if fence:
            continue
        m = re.match(r"^(#{1,6})\s+(.*?)\s*#*\s*$", line)
        if not m:
            continue
        text = re.sub(r"\[([^\]]*)\]\([^)]*\)", r"\1", m.group(2))
        text = text.replace("`", "").lower()
        s = re.sub(r"[^\w\- ]", "", text).replace(" ", "-")
        n = seen.get(s, 0)
        seen[s] = n + 1
        out.add(s if n == 0 else f"{s}-{n}")
    return out


cache, bad, checked = {}, [], 0
for dp, dns, fns in os.walk(root):
    dns[:] = [d for d in dns if d not in (".jj", ".git", "target", ".agent-session", "tmp")]
    for fn in fns:
        if not fn.endswith(".md"):
            continue
        src = os.path.join(dp, fn)
        fence = False
        for i, line in enumerate(open(src, encoding="utf-8"), 1):
            if line.lstrip().startswith("```"):
                fence = not fence
                continue
            if fence:
                continue
            line = re.sub(r"`[^`]*`", "", line)
            targets = [m.group(1) for m in re.finditer(r"\]\(([^)\s]+)\)", line)]
            m = re.match(r"^\s*\[[^\]]+\]:\s*(\S+)", line)
            if m:
                targets.append(m.group(1))
            for t in targets:
                if re.match(r"^(https?|mailto):", t) or t.startswith("#"):
                    continue
                checked += 1
                f, _, a = t.partition("#")
                p = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(dp, f))
                rel = os.path.relpath(src, root)
                if not os.path.exists(p):
                    bad.append(f"{rel}:{i}: {t}: no file")
                    continue
                if a and p.endswith(".md"):
                    if p not in cache:
                        cache[p] = slugs(p)
                    if a not in cache[p]:
                        bad.append(f"{rel}:{i}: {t}: no heading for #{a}")
print("\n".join(sorted(bad)))
print(f"xlinks: {checked} cross-file link(s) checked, {len(bad)} bad")
sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)

189:  `CONTRIBUTING.md` stub, and a message tells the other projects.
193:### feat: a cycle's state is recorded, and every end is durable
machine's. So the commands that print long output, the messaging protocol, and which agent-files
draft we carry were in `custom.md`, and a clone on fwlaptop had none of them, its session unable to
send a message. The commands themselves were a table in the README, whose reader wants to install
and use vc-x1, not change it.

#### Solution

A committed `CONTRIBUTING.md`, the project's layer, which every clone carries.

- `## Tasks`: the commands a cycle uses, in its order, each named, with what it does and when it
  runs. The README's table moves here. `custom.md`'s list of commands with long output goes, the
  Long output rule's validation, build, and test runs and unbounded logs and diffs covering it.
- `## Agents`: what an agent here reads beyond the agent-files, the draft we carry and the
  messaging protocol, with how a clone gets the messages repo.
- The README's `## Build and install` keeps installing and using vc-x1 and links to the tasks.
- `custom.md` keeps what is local alone, the standing permission for the messages Fetch. It is
  gitignored, so the commit does not carry that edit: it is named here.
- The agent-files, the draft `v0.3.1-15`: the acquaint reads `CONTRIBUTING.md > ## Agents` after
  `custom.md`, and `## custom.md` says what is not local goes in `CONTRIBUTING.md`, its why in
  `rationale.md`.

#### Acceptance check

In a fresh clone of the landed `main`, with no `custom.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` names every command
`custom.md` named for long output and the messages repo's protocol, and `AGENTS.md`'s acquaint
reads it. `vc-x1 validate` passes.

#### Deliberation

- A single-step cycle, not the first rung of the task move: the project's content is committed at
  once, a clone gets it without waiting for a ladder to land, and the task move then changes the
  command column alone.

content.text:
CONTRIBUTING.md is now required by the agent-files and created by vc-dr-apply. A workspace set up the way new ones are came out with no bad links, and full `vc-x1 validate` passes.

**What "add to the agent-files list" became.** AGENTS.md's Terminology now requires a CONTRIBUTING.md beside TODO.md and zTOC.md, with the fixed headings `## Tasks` and `## Agents`. It's not one of the files `agent-files copy` carries, since every project's content differs. Required with a fixed shape is what lets the links be real. If you meant it should literally be copied with the set, say so.

**AGENTS.md:**
- Acquaint step 1 and the `## CONTRIBUTING.md` section link `CONTRIBUTING.md#agents` and `#tasks` directly, and "when there is one" is gone.
- The rules-index line says it's required.
- The rationale says why: an optional file means a broken link wherever it's missing.

**The starter files vc-dr-apply creates:**
- **A new `CONTRIBUTING.md` stub**, with both headings, a bump row and a validate row to fill in, and the `## Agents` intro.
- **`zTOC.md`** lists it.
- **`custom.md`**, which still called itself "the project layer", now says local layer.

**The link check, by hand:**
1. I made a throwaway workspace with `vc-x1 init --repo local=...` and ran `vc-dr-apply.sh` from the working copy into it.
2. `vc-x1 validate-anchors` checked links within each file: 96 links, 0 bad. It skips links to other files.
3. A small script checked links across files, both the file and the heading. It's at `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-wink-data-prgs-rust-vc-x1/91bf53f5-cb6b-4270-b1d2-9d5537845b8c/scratchpad/xlinks.py`. # Contributing

How to build, test, and change vc-x1, for a person or an agent. What vc-x1 is, and how to install
and use it, is in [README.md](README.md). How a change is made, the cycle and its commits, is in
[AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md#cycle-protocol).

## Tasks

The project's tasks, in the order a change uses them. A change is made as a
[cycle](AGENTS.md#terminology): one commit, or a ladder of commits each called a rung, made on a
bookmark of its own and joined to `main` at the end, the Land. A task is named by its first column,
the name the agent-files use for it.

- Dev and release: the dev build is the quick debug one, for trying a change while it is made, and
  the release build is the optimized one installed as `vc-x1` at Land.

| Task | What it does | When | Command |
|---|---|---|---|
| bump | sets the version in `Cargo.toml` and refreshes `Cargo.lock`, `X.Y.Z-N` for a cycle's Nth commit and the bare `X.Y.Z` for its last ([Suffix scheme](agent-data/versioning.md#suffix-scheme)) | first, at each commit of a cycle | `cargo xtask bump X.Y.Z` |
| validate | formats the code, runs the lints, and runs every test | before each review, and before every commit | `vc-x1 validate` |
| validate fast | runs the unit tests only, changing no file | while a review iterates | `vc-x1 validate --fast` |

"""Check cross-file markdown links under a root: each target file exists, and its anchor is a heading.

Usage: python3 -I xlinks.py ROOT
Skips fenced code blocks, inline code spans, http(s)/mailto links, and same-file `#anchor` links
(vc-x1 validate-anchors covers those). Slugs follow GitHub's rule: lowercase, punctuation other
than '-' and '_' dropped, spaces to '-', and repeats numbered -1, -2, ...
"""
import os
import re
import sys

root = os.path.abspath(sys.argv[1])


def slugs(path):
    out, seen, fence = set(), {}, False
    for line in open(path, encoding="utf-8"):
        if line.lstrip().startswith("```"):
            fence = not fence
            continue
        if fence:
            continue
        m = re.match(r"^(#{1,6})\s+(.*?)\s*#*\s*$", line)
        if not m:
            continue
        text = re.sub(r"\[([^\]]*)\]\([^)]*\)", r"\1", m.group(2))
        text = text.replace("`", "").lower()
        s = re.sub(r"[^\w\- ]", "", text).replace(" ", "-")
        n = seen.get(s, 0)
        seen[s] = n + 1
        out.add(s if n == 0 else f"{s}-{n}")
    return out


cache, bad, checked = {}, [], 0
for dp, dns, fns in os.walk(root):
    dns[:] = [d for d in dns if d not in (".jj", ".git", "target", ".agent-session", "tmp")]
    for fn in fns:
        if not fn.endswith(".md"):
            continue
        src = os.path.join(dp, fn)
        fence = False
        for i, line in enumerate(open(src, encoding="utf-8"), 1):
            if line.lstrip().startswith("```"):
                fence = not fence
                continue
            if fence:
                continue
            line = re.sub(r"`[^`]*`", "", line)
            targets = [m.group(1) for m in re.finditer(r"\]\(([^)\s]+)\)", line)]
            m = re.match(r"^\s*\[[^\]]+\]:\s*(\S+)", line)
            if m:
                targets.append(m.group(1))
            for t in targets:
                if re.match(r"^(https?|mailto):", t) or t.startswith("#"):
                    continue
                checked += 1
                f, _, a = t.partition("#")
                p = os.path.normpath(os.path.join(root, f.lstrip("/")) if f.startswith("/") else os.path.join(dp, f))
                rel = os.path.relpath(src, root)
                if not os.path.exists(p):
                    bad.append(f"{rel}:{i}: {t}: no file")
                    continue
                if a and p.endswith(".md"):
                    if p not in cache:
                        cache[p] = slugs(p)
                    if a not in cache[p]:
                        bad.append(f"{rel}:{i}: {t}: no heading for #{a}")
print("\n".join(sorted(bad)))
print(f"xlinks: {checked} cross-file link(s) checked, {len(bad)} bad")
sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, handing the viewer a file to save, or using the viewer's camera, microphone, location, screen or device motion. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs (plus reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups where the model's recipe covers them) at the effort level given first, before any target (low|medium|high|xhigh|max: from few high-confidence findings to many, some uncertain; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply them to the working tree after the review. **IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list).
